roles.title: Machine-learning / modeling data scientist

what.label: What you actually do
what.md: You turn a business prediction problem into a working model. Examples: forecasting demand for 50,000 products per store so replenishment can order stock; ranking items on a home page; predicting which customers will cancel and testing which retention offer works; scoring transactions for fraud. Tasks: gather and clean data, feature engineering, train and compare models (gradient-boosted trees such as XGBoost or LightGBM remain the workhorse for tabular data; deep learning for text/images), validate offline and online, document, hand over to engineers or deploy yourself, and monitor for model drift (performance decay as the world changes). Increasingly: prototype LLM-based features (classifying support tickets, extracting fields from documents) and evaluate them. Tools: Python, SQL, scikit-learn, PyTorch, Spark, cloud platforms, experiment trackers, Git.

day.label: A typical day and week
day.md: Morning stand-up with the ML engineer and product owner; debugging data quality; training runs and code review; mid-week presentation of model results to the business owner; periodic retraining and model-monitoring reviews. About half the time is data work, not modelling (consensus).

hours.label: Hours, stress and lifestyle
hours.md: 40-50 typical, 55-60 peak around launches or incidents (consensus). Stress 3/5; on-call is uncommon unless the model is customer-facing (consensus). Hybrid is common; project cycles of 1-3 months.

profile.label: Human vs. quantitative profile
profile.md: People/communication: 3/5. Quantitative/technical: 4/5. You must be genuinely fluent in statistics and code; explaining model limits to stakeholders is also needed, but less than in product roles.

pay.label: Compensation (approximate)
pay.md:
- US: BLS median for data scientists US$120,230 (May 2025); P10 US$67,240; P90 US$199,130. Levels.fyi top-company data above apply when the job is at big tech. Amazon applied scientist (the research-leaning cousin) L4 US$247k (Levels.fyi, 9 Oct 2026). Non-tech employers (insurers, retailers) pay far less than the Levels.fyi medians suggest; BLS is the better guide for the average market.
- UK: banks' data science graduate schemes advertise GBP 42,000 (NatWest, 12-month data science programme, 2027 intake) and GBP 48,500 (Lloyds Banking Group Data Science & AI scheme, 2 years); Capital One UK GBP 46,500-55,500 plus GBP 5,000 joining bonus on its technology programme (employer listings, September 2026). Mid-career London: GBP 60-90k (Pocketwise, a general site, weak); senior GBP 70-100k nationally.
- Italy: junior roughly EUR 29-42k gross (Glassdoor Feb 2026 EUR 26-33k; NettoCalc Milan EUR 42,000 for 0-3 years, a weaker aggregator); Generali Italia listing for a junior innovation and data analytics role EUR 36,000 (undated). Mid-career Italy and senior: no reliable data found beyond Levels.fyi's Italy 75th percentile EUR 60k and 90th EUR 74k (all levels, n=23). Hays Italy's 2026 guide gives EUR 56,360 as the average RAL across all professions surveyed, not data science.
- Switzerland (for reference): Zurich senior data scientist median CHF 150,748 (n=16); all-levels CHF 116,413 (Levels.fyi, 9 Oct 2026). Singapore: median SGD 120k (all levels); Skillup (2026, MyCareersFuture data from March 2024) gives SGD 60k at 0-2 years, 105k at 2-5, 140k at 5-8, 180k at 8+ (base).

path.label: Career path
path.md: Junior/associate data scientist (0-2 years) → data scientist (2-5) → senior (5-8) → staff/principal or lead (8+). Many people move to "ML engineer" or "AI engineer" at the mid-level because that title currently carries more demand.

exits.label: Exit opportunities
exits.md: After 2-3 years: ML engineer, AI engineer, data scientist at a larger employer, product analytics, quant research (with strong maths, see Finance). After 7-10 years: lead/head of data science, ML engineering management, AI product, consulting, founder.

tiers.label: Tier list of employers
tiers.md:
Tier groupings reflect industry consensus and practitioner perception, not objective fact.
- Tier 1: big tech ML organisations and top ML-driven scale-ups (Google, Meta, Netflix, Stripe, Spotify, Zalando, Booking.com). Large data, mature MLOps, ML-engineer colleagues; very selective.
- Tier 2: banks and insurers with real analytics functions (Capital One, JPMorgan, Lloyds, NatWest, Admiral, Allianz), retailers with data platforms, telecoms, energy majors (Enel, Eni), larger Italian and European corporates. Real problems and good training, slower tooling, more governance.
- Tier 3: consultancies' delivery teams, mid-market firms and IT-services outsourcers where "data scientist" can mean reporting and light modelling.

enter.label: How to enter
enter.md:
- Degrees: bachelor's in computer science, statistics, mathematics, physics, engineering or economics; a master's in data science, statistics, machine learning or an applied field is the common path and is expected for most European roles. A PhD is not needed for most modelling roles. UK banks typically require a 2:1 in a STEM subject (NatWest). Lloyds states no minimum degree classification but expects demonstrable technical skills and does not sponsor visas.
- Programmes: NatWest Graduate Trainee Data Science (12 months, GBP 42,000, 2027 intake); Lloyds Data Science and AI graduate scheme (2 years, 2 year-long placements incl. fraud and credit risk); Capital One UK technology programme; UK bank intakes typically run September to January with applications closing in autumn, so 2027 intake rounds are running now. Admiral's analytics/data science scheme (Cardiff): two 25-month programmes, 2026 intake deadline 26 Oct 2025 (listing).
- Interviews: online assessment (logic, maths), SQL and Python coding test, then case or technical interviews on statistics and model evaluation; take-home projects are common at start-ups. Italian consultancies describe an online test, SQL/Python technical interview and optional case (Glassdoor candidate reports on Accenture and Reply, anecdotal).
- Certifications: cloud ones (AWS, Azure, Google) help only slightly; kaggle rankings and projects matter more. Skills: Python, SQL, scikit-learn and gradient boosting, validation and leakage, basic cloud and Git, communication. Portfolio: an end-to-end project with deployment (even a small API), a forecasting or fraud project on public data, a GitHub repo with clean code.
- Common mistakes: modelling without checking the data, leakage, optimising accuracy instead of the business metric, building huge deep-learning models where a simple baseline works.
- Alternative routes: analyst → data scientist; software engineers moving into ML; non-target schools can use competitions, open-source contributions and internships at mid-sized firms.
- Entry difficulty: 4/5.

downsides.label: Honest downsides and who it is NOT a good fit for
downsides.md: Much of the day is data cleaning, and many models never reach production; the title is being replaced by ML/AI engineer, which asks for software skills; entry hiring has tightened (see 2.1). Not a good fit if you dislike coding or messy data, or want research freedom (that is 3.6).

roles.title: Decision scientist / operations research analyst

what.label: What you actually do
what.md: You build mathematical models that tell a business what to do. Concrete examples: decide which warehouse serves which customers, design delivery routes for 500 vans, schedule crews and aircraft, set airline fares and seat limits per flight (revenue management), size safety stock, simulate a new hospital layout, optimise power dispatch. Method: formulate the problem (objective, decision variables, constraints), solve with a solver or heuristic, test against simulation and historical data, deliver a tool or recommendation. Tools: Python, a modelling library or solver (Gurobi, CPLEX, OR-Tools, Pyomo), simulation software, SQL, sometimes Julia/AMPL; Excel remains common at the business end. Deliverables: optimisation engines, what-if tools, business cases quantifying savings.

day.label: A typical day and week
day.md: Mix of modelling (50%) and stakeholder work (clarifying constraints with planners, validating that the model "feels right" to the people who run operations). Weekly cadence of progress reviews; occasional site visits to warehouses or hangars.

hours.label: Hours, stress and lifestyle
hours.md: 38-45 typical, 50-55 peak at go-live or planning season (consensus). Stress 2/5 (occasional crunch at go-live or when an operational crisis hits). Mostly desk work, light travel to sites. Hybrid common. A BLS note: most operations research analysts work full time.

profile.label: Human vs. quantitative profile
profile.md: People/communication: 3/5. Quantitative/technical: 5/5 at research-heavy teams; 4/5 for analyst roles. Mathematical modelling is the core, but the model only matters if planners trust it.

pay.label: Compensation (approximate)
pay.md:
- US: BLS operations research analysts median US$88,940 (May 2025); P10 US$57,060; P90 US$159,910. Growth 12% 2025-35, about 7,500 openings a year. Entry roughly US$55-75k typical outside tech (state career portals show about US$48k for entry-level; older and weak). Amazon-type optimisation scientist roles in big tech fall in the applied-scientist band (3.6); not verified for OR-specific titles.
- UK: a careers-profile figure of GBP 25-29k starting and GBP 40-80k+ for experienced operational researchers (undated, probably older); UK Government Operational Research Service (GORS) sandwich-placement advert Nov 2025 GBP 22,699-31,324 pro rata; Fast Stream operational researchers start around GBP 27k (older figure). ITJobsWatch "decision scientist" median GBP 82,500 (6 months to 10 May 2025, only 2 salaries quoted; anecdotal).
- Italy: no reliable data found. Continental Europe and Asia: no reliable data found.

path.label: Career path
path.md: OR analyst/associate (0-3) → senior analyst/scientist (3-7) → lead/principal scientist, optimisation architect or planning manager (7-12). Public-sector route: GORS analyst → senior → head of profession.

exits.label: Exit opportunities
exits.md: After 2-3 years: supply-chain planning and analytics, data science, consulting (operations), software vendors of planning tools. After 7-10 years: head of supply-chain analytics, product owner of an optimisation product, consulting partner track, operations leadership.

tiers.label: Tier list of employers
tiers.md:
Tier groupings reflect industry consensus and practitioner perception, not objective fact. Employer names below are general industry knowledge, not verified in this round.
- Tier 1: large logistics/e-commerce optimisation groups, major airlines' revenue-management and network-planning teams, planning-software vendors (Gurobi, Kinaxis, Blue Yonder, o9, FICO), and defence/government research bodies. Deepest OR work and best pay; few entry posts.
- Tier 2: manufacturers, retailers, utilities and grid operators (Enel and Terna in Italy), banks' operations units, consultancies' supply-chain practices.
- Tier 3: general operations analyst roles where "analyst" means Excel reporting.

enter.label: How to enter
enter.md:
- Degrees: industrial/management engineering, mathematics, applied mathematics, operations research, computer science, physics; a master's (OR, industrial engineering, applied maths) is the usual route for modelling roles, and BLS says a bachelor's is the minimum with some employers preferring a master's. Italy is strong in the field through engineering faculties (e.g. gestionale/industrial engineering) - consensus; I did not verify programme details.
- Programmes and calendars: UK government GORS via Fast Stream (applications open autumn); corporate supply-chain graduate programmes follow the usual autumn-to-spring cycle.
- Interviews: optimisation modelling case (formulate a vehicle routing or scheduling problem on a whiteboard), probability and statistics, coding (Python), behavioural.
- Certifications: INFORMS Certified Analytics Professional (CAP) now has three tiers: CAP-Essentials (early career, no eligibility requirements), CAP-Pro, and CAP-Expert (requires an advanced degree with 2 years of analytics experience, or bachelor's with 4, or 8 years' experience). They are recognised in the US more than in Europe; they help rather than decide.
- Skills and portfolio: linear/integer programming, simulation, solver use, a project such as a delivery-route optimiser or a staff-rostering model on open data.
- Common mistakes: building elegant models without involving the planners; ignoring data quality; not quantifying business value.
- Alternative routes: logistics or supply-chain graduates add a quantitative master's or a strong Python/solver portfolio; data analysts can move via planning teams.
- Entry difficulty: 3/5 (smaller field, specific skills, but fewer applicants than product data science).

downsides.label: Honest downsides and who it is NOT a good fit for
downsides.md: Niche job market (a small number of employers use real optimisation); many roles are labelled "analyst" and become reporting; adoption by planners can be slow; pay is lower than product/ML data science outside big tech. Not a good fit if you dislike formal mathematics or want fast-moving product work.

roles.title: Statistician / biostatistician

what.label: What you actually do
what.md: In pharma or at a CRO (contract research organisation, which runs clinical trials for drug companies), you are the person who makes sure a trial's conclusions are statistically valid. Tasks: write the statistical analysis plan (the pre-agreed recipe for analysing the trial), calculate sample size, specify the randomisation, review the case report forms, analyse efficacy and safety endpoints, handle missing data, produce tables and figures for the clinical study report, and answer regulators' questions. Statistical programmers (a close neighbour role) write the SAS or R code to produce datasets in CDISC standards (SDTM/ADaM) and the outputs. In official statistics (ISTAT, ONS, Eurostat) you design surveys, weight and estimate, check quality and publish national figures such as inflation or unemployment. In public health, you analyse cohort and registry data. Tools: SAS (still dominant in regulated pharma), R, Python growing; survival analysis, mixed models, Bayesian methods.

day.label: A typical day and week
day.md: Mix of programming and analysis (40%), documentation and review (30%), meetings with clinicians and data managers (20%), and waiting for data (10%). Workload peaks around database lock and submission deadlines; calmer in between (consensus). In national statistics offices the rhythm follows publication calendars.

hours.label: Hours, stress and lifestyle
hours.md: 38-45 typical; 50+ during database lock or regulatory submission (consensus). Stress 2/5 (occasional crunch around deadlines; accuracy pressure because errors affect regulatory decisions). Remote or hybrid is widespread, particularly at CROs (consensus). Little travel. Public sector hours are 36-40 with strong job security in Italy and the UK (consensus).

profile.label: Human vs. quantitative profile
profile.md: People/communication: 3/5. Quantitative/technical: 5/5. Statistical correctness is the job; you also need to explain trade-offs to physicians and regulators.

pay.label: Compensation (approximate)
pay.md:
- US: BLS statisticians median US$105,650 (May 2025); P10 US$64,000; P90 US$174,050; highest-paying industry computer systems design (median US$167,180), federal government US$132,620, R&D in life/physical/engineering sciences US$130,590, healthcare US$100,900. Levels.fyi lists Biostatistician as a top-paying data-scientist-adjacent title at US$143,000 median (9 Oct 2026; sample not disclosed). Entry-level biostatistician: no reliable US figure found in this round.
- UK: Payscale (2026) average biostatistician in London GBP 49,132 (range GBP 33-58k), early-career London GBP 33,971; advertised CRO statistician roles GBP 45-55k (experienced late-phase and senior roles; undated listings); ITJobsWatch biostatistics median GBP 80,000 (6 months to 25 July 2026, 6 salaries; anecdotal). Government: ONS Higher Statistical Officer GBP 35,144 (advert closing 6 January 2026); GBP 30-35k (advert closing September 2025); ONS statistician about GBP 39.4k (2024 advert); senior statistician about GBP 43.0k; Fast Stream Statistician starts around GBP 28-31k (older figures).
- Italy: no reliable data found for biostatistician pay. ISTAT hires through public competitions (concorsi) with a nationally set pay scale; 2026 competition for 54 researchers and 46 technologists (third level, master's degree required; a doctorate or documented research experience counted favourably) closed 22 January 2026 (ISTAT, accessed Oct 2026); pay in the call text not retrieved. GSK Siena's 2026 statistics/biostatistics graduate programme: pay not stated.
- Continental Europe elsewhere and Asia: no reliable data found.

path.label: Career path
path.md: Junior/associate biostatistician or statistical programmer (0-3 years) → biostatistician / senior (3-6) → principal / associate director (7-10 at CROs; IQVIA's associate-director postings ask for a master's with seven years' CRO/pharma experience, or a doctorate with five) → director/VP biostatistics. Academic/public-health track: research statistician → lecturer. Official-statistics track: statistical officer → statistician → senior statistician.

exits.label: Exit opportunities
exits.md: After 2-3 years: another CRO or pharma company, regulatory agencies, health-data science, real-world evidence, statistical programming → data engineering, clinical data science. After 7-10 years: head of biostatistics, clinical development leadership, HEOR or market-access modelling (cross-reference Healthcare/Pharma), consultancy, regulator.

tiers.label: Tier list of employers
tiers.md:
Tier groupings reflect industry consensus and practitioner perception, not objective fact.
- Tier 1: large pharma (Roche, Novartis, AstraZeneca, GSK, Novo Nordisk, Sanofi, Pfizer, MSD, J&J, Lilly, Bayer) and top biotech; regulators (FDA, EMA) and elite academic trial units (e.g. the UK's MRC/university units). Better pay and scientific influence, hardest to enter (Roche and AXA are the top Zurich payers on Levels.fyi data scientist pages, 2026).
- Tier 2: large CROs (IQVIA, Parexel, Syneos, ICON, Thermo Fisher PPD, Fortrea) and mid-size pharma (Italian examples: Chiesi, Menarini, Zambon; names from general knowledge, not verified for biostatistics). Large entry intake, structured training, more repetitive workload and billable-hour pressure.
- Tier 3: small CROs, hospitals and general statistical consultancies; public-sector offices (ISTAT, ONS) sit apart: lower pay, high stability, good work-life balance, meaningful but less commercial work.

enter.label: How to enter
enter.md:
- Degrees: a master's in statistics or biostatistics is the standard ticket (BLS: statisticians typically need a master's, some entry jobs accept a bachelor's; IQVIA's UK graduate postings (2021-22) accepted a BSc or MSc with six months of experience). Italy: Laurea Magistrale in Biostatistica (Milano-Bicocca, taught in Italian, admission interview) or Statistical Methods and Applications (Sapienza, in English), or Statistics and Data Science at Florence with a Biostatistics curriculum (university pages, accessed Oct 2026). GSK Siena's 2026 programme requires an MSc with a strong biostatistics or medical statistics focus, R assessed, and fluent English and Italian. Mathematics, physics, engineering and economics graduates enter with a statistics master's.
- Programmes and calendar: pharma graduate programmes recruit on a rolling or annual autumn basis (GSK is rolling); CRO graduate roles hire continuously; the UK Government Statistical Service Fast Stream applies a 3.5-year scheme and requires a 2:1 in a numerate subject with taught statistics (GOV.UK/Civil Service). ISTAT hires only through formal concorsi, announced irregularly; applications via the InPA portal, which requires a digital identity (SPID, CIE or CNS).
- Interviews: statistics theory (confidence intervals, hypothesis tests, survival analysis, regression), SAS or R coding test, case about trial design (how many patients? what endpoint?), behavioural. Public-sector roles use written exams or the concorso format.
- Certifications: Chartered Statistician (Royal Statistical Society) and the ASA's PStat are valued by employers, particularly in the UK and US, but not required to enter (general knowledge, not verified this round). SAS certifications help marginally.
- Skills and portfolio: R and SAS, CDISC basics, clinical trial concepts, survival analysis; a project analysing open trial data.
- Common mistakes: applying with machine learning projects only and no inference background; weak SAS/R; ignoring regulatory context.
- Alternative routes: a maths or biology bachelor's plus a one-year statistics MSc; statistical programmer → biostatistician; data analysts in healthcare moving via a part-time master's.
- Entry difficulty: 3/5 (master's required, but CROs hire many people).

downsides.label: Honest downsides and who it is NOT a good fit for
downsides.md: Work is regulated and procedural; innovation is slower; SAS and rigid documentation can feel old-fashioned; CRO workload spikes and billable pressure; pay in Europe is moderate. Not a good fit if you want fast-moving product environments or if you dislike formal documentation and statistics theory.

roles.title: Data scientist in banking and insurance (credit, fraud, pricing)
roles.shortName: Data scientist in banking and insurance

what.label: What you actually do
what.md: You build and maintain models that decide money questions: probability of default for loan applicants (credit scoring), the expected loss reserve under accounting standard IFRS 9, transaction fraud scores, customer lifetime value, claims-severity and pricing models for car or home insurance, anti-money-laundering alert ranking. Banks usually separate model development (the data scientist) from independent model validation and from model risk oversight; every model needs documentation, back-testing and explainability for regulators. Tools: Python, SQL, SAS (still common in credit risk), gradient boosting, logistic regression and scorecards, cloud platforms. Deliverables: model code and documentation, monitoring reports, committee presentations.

day.label: A typical day and week
day.md: Model build and testing (40%), documentation and governance (25%), data checks (20%), stakeholder meetings with risk and business owners (15%). Regulatory deadlines and audit findings cause bursts of documentation work.

hours.label: Hours, stress and lifestyle
hours.md: 38-45 typical, 50 peak near regulatory deadlines (consensus). Stress 3/5: steady deadlines, accountability for model failures, but far from investment-banking hours. Hybrid is standard in UK and European banks, fully on-site expectations rising in US banks (consensus). Little travel.

profile.label: Human vs. quantitative profile
profile.md: People/communication: 3/5. Quantitative/technical: 4/5. Explaining a model to a risk committee and validators counts as much as its accuracy.

pay.label: Compensation (approximate)
pay.md:
- US: US$150,000 base for Barclays' 2027 Quantitative Analytics graduate programme in New York (a quant-risk role; listing); generic data scientist data from BLS (US$120,230 median; insurance carriers and credit intermediation employ 16% of US data scientists). Entry-level for a credit-risk data scientist outside quant roles: no reliable figure found.
- UK: NatWest Risk Modelling graduate trainee GBP 37,500 (2027 intake; older cohorts GBP 33.5-35k), NatWest Data Science graduate trainee GBP 42,000, Lloyds Data Science and AI GBP 48,500, Capital One UK GBP 46,500-55,500 plus GBP 5,000 joining bonus (technology and strategy analyst graduate programmes, intake Sept 2027), Aviva Data and Analytics pathway GBP 33,200 (closed). Levels.fyi: NatWest data scientist median total GBP 48.8k (April 2026), Lloyds GBP 48.5k; JPMorgan London data scientists average ~GBP 144.9k (all levels, thin).
- Italy: Generali Italia junior innovation and data analytics role EUR 36,000 (undated listing); UniCredit's Munich trainee programme advertises from EUR 59,761 gross (a German salary, from a different trainee listing); Levels.fyi Italy top payers Enel EUR 56.8k and Prima EUR 56.1k, Generali EUR 35.8k (all levels, small samples). Intesa Sanpaolo's data science offering found this round was internship-level (audit data science internship, May 2026).
- Elsewhere: Singapore bank data scientists (DBS, others) senior roughly SGD 12-16k a month per Skillup (2026, weak); GovTech median SGD 117,421 (Levels.fyi, Feb 2026). Insurers in Zurich: AXA CHF 123,942 (Levels.fyi, thin).

path.label: Career path
path.md: Graduate/associate modeller (0-2) → data scientist / model developer (2-5) → senior / VP (5-9) → head of credit analytics, chief data scientist or model risk head (10+). Insurance: pricing analyst → pricing data scientist → head of pricing; actuarial qualification opens another ladder.

exits.label: Exit opportunities
exits.md: After 2-3 years: fintech or big-tech risk teams, consulting (risk analytics), model validation, credit strategy, or other lenders. After 7-10 years: chief risk officer track, head of data science, fintech leadership.

tiers.label: Tier list of employers
tiers.md:
Tier groupings reflect industry consensus and practitioner perception, not objective fact.
- Tier 1: data-driven lenders and large global banks with significant modelling teams (Capital One, JPMorgan, Barclays, HSBC), and leading insurers/pricing houses (Admiral, Allianz, AXA, Zurich, Aviva). Strong tooling, best pay inside finance.
- Tier 2: high-street and national banks (NatWest, Lloyds, Intesa Sanpaolo, UniCredit) and Italian insurers (Generali, UnipolSai). Large intakes, rotational programmes, stronger governance burden.
- Tier 3: regional banks, smaller insurers, and outsourced analytics providers; smaller teams and less modern stack.

enter.label: How to enter
enter.md:
- Degrees: STEM (maths, statistics, physics, engineering, computer science) or economics with quantitative focus; NatWest requires a 2:1 in STEM; Admiral lists maths, physics, engineering, chemistry or biology; a master's is common but not required for UK graduate schemes. For Italy a laurea magistrale in statistics, economics, mathematics or data science is typical.
- Programmes and calendar: UK schemes open August-October for next September, with early deadlines (Capital One closed 6 Sept 2026; Admiral's 2026 intake closed 26 Oct 2025; Aviva's pathway has closed; Allianz Ireland's data analytics programme closes 11 Oct 2026). Italian banks and insurers use a mix of graduate programmes (Intesa Sanpaolo SLAM, a 24-month international programme; Generali's international programme) and internships/stage; UniCredit Group runs a 12-month rotational trainee programme with a 2026 "data scientist for agentic AI and banking" track in Munich.
- Interviews: online tests (logic, numeracy), coding (SQL/Python) tests, case study on risk or pricing, technical interview on regression and classification metrics (AUC, Gini, KS), behavioural.
- Certifications: not required; for insurance, actuarial exams (UK Institute and Faculty of Actuaries, Italian Albo) are a different path; FRM/PRM are sometimes seen in risk functions (general knowledge).
- Skills and portfolio: logistic regression and gradient boosting, scorecard development, calibration, explainability (SHAP), fairness testing, SQL; a credit-scoring project using public data with proper validation.
- Common mistakes: ignoring interpretability and regulation; treating bank data as clean; overselling deep learning.
- Alternative routes: analysts in risk or finance with a coding upgrade; actuarial trainees adding machine learning; from the Lloyds scheme, which does not require a particular degree classification.
- Entry difficulty: 3/5.

downsides.label: Honest downsides and who it is NOT a good fit for
downsides.md: Heavy governance and documentation slow delivery; legacy systems; models limited to explainable techniques; pay at the entry level is much lower than big tech. Not a good fit if you want rapid experimentation or cutting-edge ML, or if you dislike regulation and process.

roles.title: Applied scientist / research data scientist (PhD-track)

what.label: What you actually do
what.md: You tackle open-ended problems where off-the-shelf methods are not enough, and you aim for a measurable product or business impact. Typical Amazon-style applied scientist work: improving search ranking with a new deep-learning approach, building a better demand-forecasting model, training or fine-tuning language models for a shopping assistant, or designing a causal model of how a price change affects demand. Economists in tech do similar work with econometrics: for example estimating how advertising affects sales, or designing an auction. Tasks: literature review, prototyping in Python and PyTorch, offline evaluation, then collaborating with software engineers to put the model into production, plus writing papers or internal research memos. Deliverables: models and methods, experiments, papers, patents.

day.label: A typical day and week
day.md: Reading papers and running training jobs (40%), writing code and analysis (30%), meetings with engineers and product partners (20%), writing (10%). Project cycles of 3-9 months (consensus). Heavy GPU/compute scheduling; waiting for runs.

hours.label: Hours, stress and lifestyle
hours.md: 40-50 typical, 55-60 around paper deadlines or launches (consensus). Stress 3/5: high expectations to deliver impact, performance reviews, uncertainty about whether research will work. Hybrid. Conference travel (NeurIPS, ICML, KDD, EC) is a perk.

profile.label: Human vs. quantitative profile
profile.md: People/communication: 2/5. Quantitative/technical: 5/5. Deep technical competence is the core; you still need to convince engineers to adopt your method.

pay.label: Compensation (approximate)
pay.md:
- US: Amazon applied scientist L4 US$247k, L5 US$323k, L6 US$413k, L7 US$653k total compensation (Levels.fyi, 9 Oct 2026, 107 submissions; median all levels US$335k). Another Levels.fyi snapshot (18 Aug 2026) shows L5 US$324k and L6 US$407k. Stock makes up a large share at senior levels. Google data scientist L3 US$196k, L4 US$281k, L5 US$380k (not research scientists; research scientist ladders were not retrieved).
- UK: no reliable data found for applied scientist roles (London figures on Levels.fyi are all-levels data scientist data: median GBP 91k). UK skilled-worker route: the going rate for SOC 2433 (statistical data scientists) is GBP 55,100 (GOV.UK, updated April 2026, from the project's earlier research); new entrants can be paid 70% of the going rate if above the general floor.
- Continental Europe: Amazon's Berlin applied scientist posting (employer-stated, 16 June 2026, from project research) asks for a PhD or a master's plus four years' experience; pay not stated. Italy: no reliable data found for applied scientist pay. Asia: Tokyo's Sakana AI JPY 21.1m and PayPay JPY 18.4m for data scientists (Levels.fyi, 9 Oct 2026, thin); Singapore Grab SGD 160k.

path.label: Career path
path.md: Applied scientist I/II (0-4 years after PhD or MSc plus experience; Amazon L4/L5) → senior applied scientist (L6, ~5-9 years) → principal scientist (L7) or research manager (10+ years). Economists follow a similar scientist ladder.

exits.label: Exit opportunities
exits.md: After 2-3 years: research scientist at other labs, ML engineering, startups (founding technical), AI labs (see the AI branch). After 7-10 years: principal scientist, head of science, academia (professor), startup CTO or founder, quant research (with strong maths).

tiers.label: Tier list of employers
tiers.md:
Tier groupings reflect industry consensus and practitioner perception, not objective fact.
- Tier 1: frontier research groups at Google (Research/DeepMind), Meta, Microsoft Research, Amazon, Apple, and elite AI labs (see AI branch). Highest pay, strongest peers, hardest entry.
- Tier 2: product-focused science teams at Booking.com, Spotify, Zalando, Uber, Airbnb, Netflix, Adyen and marketplaces; corporate research labs (Siemens, Bosch, IBM, SAP); central banks' and policy institutions' economists.
- Tier 3: applied research in banks, pharma and consulting; smaller labs. Less publication freedom, more business constraints.

enter.label: How to enter
enter.md:
- Degrees: PhD (or an excellent master's with research output) in computer science, statistics, machine learning, economics, operations research or physics. Amazon's mid-level applied scientist posting asks for a PhD, or a master's with four or more years of CS/ML experience, and 3+ years of model-building experience; many postings also list publications at top conferences or patents (Amazon postings, accessed Oct 2026; Berlin posting 16 June 2026). Google's research scientist internships require current enrolment in a master's or PhD with research experience preferred (Google listings, 2026). IMC London lists a graduate Machine Learning Researcher role requiring an MSc, PhD preferred (employer listing, Oct 2026).
- Programmes and calendar: research internships for PhD students (Google, Microsoft, Meta, Amazon) recruit in autumn for the next summer; full-time applied scientist hiring is continuous; new-grad research scientist posts are rare.
- Interviews: a research talk, ML fundamentals and coding, statistics, and a system or experimental design discussion; economists face theory and applied microeconomics.
- Certifications: do not matter.
- Skills and portfolio: publications at top venues, open-source code, strong mathematics, PyTorch, ability to ship.
- Common mistakes: expecting a pure research job (business impact is the metric); weak engineering; confusing a coursework master's with research credentials. A one- or two-year master's without publications is a weak route to this role (prior project research notes an effective near-zero hit rate for research-scientist roles from such programmes, a claim I treat as unverified).
- Alternative routes: start as a data scientist or ML engineer and move into science after a part-time PhD, or via research-oriented master's theses and publications; economics PhDs enter via tech economist roles.
- Entry difficulty: 5/5.

downsides.label: Honest downsides and who it is NOT a good fit for
downsides.md: Needs 4-6 years of PhD training at lower pay; few openings; pressure to turn research into products; the best research roles are moving into frontier AI labs. Not a good fit if you want a business-facing career quickly or do not enjoy academic-style research.

roles.title: Data science consultant

what.label: What you actually do
what.md: You deliver analytics and AI projects for clients. Typical engagement: a retailer wants to forecast demand, a bank wants a churn model, an energy company wants predictive maintenance. You scope the problem with the client, access and clean their data, prototype a model, build a proof of concept, and present results to executives, ideally with a path to production. Roles range from hands-on data scientist inside a strategy consultancy's AI unit (McKinsey QuantumBlack, BCG X) to analytics consultants in the Big Four and IT integrators (Deloitte, Accenture, Capgemini, Reply, Bip). Tools: Python, SQL, cloud platforms (Azure, AWS, GCP), Power BI/Tableau, PowerPoint.

day.label: A typical day and week
day.md: Client-site or video calls in the morning, data work and modelling mid-day, slides and weekly steering meeting with the client, plus staffing and proposal activities. Mostly 3-6 month projects, with client changes common. Postings for McKinsey QuantumBlack ask for willingness to travel and to attend meetings outside traditional business hours (McKinsey job listings, 2026).

hours.label: Hours, stress and lifestyle
hours.md: 45-55 typical, 60+ before steering committees (consensus). A former McKinsey consultant said data scientists there work slightly fewer hours than generalist consultants, unless on site with the client (PrepLounge forum answer, 2022, anecdotal). Stress 4/5: client deadlines, shifting scope, "up or out" or utilisation pressure at strategy firms; IT-consulting body shops run at 3/5 (consensus). Travel: variable; a BCG Hong Kong posting lists travel based on client needs; a McKinsey Lisbon posting lists willingness to travel. Hybrid with client-site days.

profile.label: Human vs. quantitative profile
profile.md: People/communication: 4/5. Quantitative/technical: 4/5. You need both: clients buy the story, not the model.

pay.label: Compensation (approximate)
pay.md:
- US: BCG data scientist ladder on Levels.fyi US$166k (L1) to US$265k (L5) total compensation (updated 7 June 2025, small sample); no reliable figure for QuantumBlack or Big Four entry-level data scientists found.
- UK: no reliable data found for data science consultant pay at strategy firms; Big Four and integrators typically pay graduate-level salaries comparable to other consulting entry roles (not verified here).
- Italy: no firm-specific figures found. Deloitte Italy junior consultants about EUR 30k gross per an aggregator (not data-science-specific, weak); Glassdoor (Feb 2026, 214 salaries) junior data scientist Italy about EUR 29k; NettoCalc Milan junior EUR 42k. Accenture, Deloitte, Reply and BIP post junior data scientist roles in Milan without stating pay.
- Asia: no reliable data found.

path.label: Career path
path.md: Analyst/associate data scientist (0-2) → consultant / data scientist II (2-4) → senior consultant / engagement manager (4-8) → principal, associate partner, partner (8-14 at strategy firms; different at IT firms). At QuantumBlack-type units, ladders are Data Scientist I/II, Senior Data Scientist, then Principal/Associate Partner (McKinsey listings use "Data Scientist I", "Data Scientist II", "Senior Data Scientist I").

exits.label: Exit opportunities
exits.md: After 2-3 years: in-house data science at a client; product or strategy roles; ML engineering; PhD. After 7-10 years: head of analytics or Chief Data Officer, partner, startup leadership.

tiers.label: Tier list of employers
tiers.md:
Tier groupings reflect industry consensus and practitioner perception, not objective fact.
- Tier 1: McKinsey (QuantumBlack), BCG (BCG X), Bain (advanced analytics). Prestige, very strong colleagues, high pay and the hardest entry; hours are long.
- Tier 2: Deloitte, PwC, EY, KPMG, Accenture, Capgemini and specialist data and AI firms. Large intakes, more varied quality, more delivery-style work.
- Tier 3: Italian and European boutiques and integrators such as Reply and Bip (which says it recruits graduates through those with two years' experience), small agencies and outsourcers. Rapid learning, long hours for pay, little prestige.

enter.label: How to enter
enter.md:
- Degrees: STEM bachelor's or master's (computer science, statistics, maths, engineering, physics); QuantumBlack postings list a bachelor's, master's or PhD in computer science, machine learning, applied statistics, mathematics, engineering or AI, and ask for statistical sampling and machine-learning fluency. BCG X postings vary: a data science internship exists, and other posts ask for 2-4 years' experience.
- Programmes and calendar: strategy-firm recruiting is autumn-driven; IT consultancies hire continuously. Accenture Milan's process: online assessment (logic, maths), technical test on SQL and Python, optional case study; Reply Milan: SQL and Python questions then reasoning (Glassdoor reports, anecdotal).
- Interviews: case interviews (business problem structuring), coding tests, machine learning questions and a "tell us about a project" discussion.
- Certifications: cloud certificates (Azure, AWS, Google) are viewed positively at Big Four and integrators; not at strategy firms.
- Skills and portfolio: a portfolio of client-style projects, strong slides, structured problem solving, English fluency.
- Common mistakes: building models without stakeholder buy-in; ignoring the "so what"; accepting a job at an IT body shop expecting data science work.
- Alternative routes: analyst-to-consultant moves; PhD graduates enter strategy firms' expert tracks; company switchers from industry.
- Entry difficulty: 4/5 at Tier 1; 3/5 elsewhere.

downsides.label: Honest downsides and who it is NOT a good fit for
downsides.md: Long hours and travel; the project-based work means shallow involvement in the final product; many projects stop at proofs of concept; pay at Tier 3 firms is low for the workload. Not a good fit if you want depth in one domain or predictable hours.

roles.title: Data analyst / business analyst (generalist, in-house)

what.label: What you actually do
what.md: You are the person a department comes to with questions. You write SQL against the warehouse, wrangle Excel files, build and maintain recurring reports, define KPIs with stakeholders, run one-off analyses (why did churn rise, which stores underperform, what is the size of an opportunity) and present findings in decks or dashboards. Tools: SQL, Excel, a BI tool, increasingly Python or R for cleaning and basic stats, and AI assistants for drafting queries. Deliverables: weekly dashboards, a 5-slide readout, a metric dictionary, a cleaned dataset. UK advertised skills (Oct 2026): SQL, BI, Power BI, Python, Excel.

day.label: A typical day and week
day.md: Morning check that overnight refreshes ran and numbers reconcile; a stand-up with a finance or marketing partner; two or three ad hoc requests; a block of deep work on an analysis; afternoon review of a draft with a manager. Weekly cadence: Monday reports out, midweek analysis, Friday readout. Month-end and quarter-end bring reconciliation and board packs. Much of the effort is chasing definitions and bad data, not clever modelling (dbt survey: poor data quality is the top challenge).

hours.label: Hours, stress and lifestyle
hours.md: Typically 37-42 hours a week; peaks 45-55 at reporting deadlines (Prospects: usually 37-40 hours, longer near deadlines). Stress 3/5 (2 in stable teams): steady deadlines, stakeholders who want answers "today". Hybrid is the norm in UK/Europe (2-3 office days; practitioner observation); US varies by employer; little travel. Italy: contracted 40 hours is common with less remote work than UK (general knowledge, unverified).

profile.label: Human vs. quantitative profile
profile.md: People/communication: 3/5. Quantitative/technical: 3/5. The job rewards translating a vague question into a precise query and a result into a decision; advanced statistics is rarely needed.

pay.label: Compensation (approximate)
pay.md:
- UK: starting about £28,000-£32,000, experienced £35,000-£50,000, senior £50,000-£65,000+ (Prospects, 2026 page; TargetJobs gives about £28,000 on graduate schemes, about £40,000 experienced). Adverts: median £52,500 (ITJobsWatch, 6 months to 9 Oct 2026, all levels). Levels.fyi UK median total comp £50,568 (n=125, Oct 2026).
- US: no clean entry figure found; Levels.fyi median total comp $110,000 (25th $85,000, 75th $145,000; n=1,037, Oct 2026, tech-skewed), top payers Meta ($260,000), Amazon ($203,000), Walmart ($155,000). Entry about $60,000-$80,000 base (author estimate, unverified); senior $130,000+ (Levels.fyi 75th-90th percentile $145,000-$185,000).
- Italy: Deloitte junior data analyst Milan/Cagliari EUR 27,900 (Indeed listing, Aug 2026); SDG Group junior data analyst Milan EUR 26,000-28,000 (June 2026 listing); Indeed Italy average base EUR 30,854, Milan EUR 31,395 (n=77, July 2026); Levels.fyi Italy median total EUR 44,928 (n=21, Oct 2026; an earlier search snippet showed EUR 34,000, so sources disagree). Hays Italy Salary Guide 2026 reports all-role average RAL (gross annual salary) of EUR 40,560 for 2-5 years' experience and EUR 59,700 for 5-10 years. Italian figures usually include the 13th/14th monthly payments in RAL.
- Asia/Middle East: Singapore median total SGD 75,419 (Levels.fyi, n=38); Hong Kong median HKD 45,000 per month, range 23,000-70,000 (Morgan McKinley 2026; currency presumed HKD); Dubai median AED 203,998 total (Levels.fyi, n=15, thin); Tokyo foreign-multinational BI/data analyst adverts JPY 6.5-8.5m (Michael Page Japan listings, Oct 2026); India median INR 1,469,274 total (Levels.fyi, n=402).

path.label: Career path
path.md: Junior/associate analyst (0-2 years), analyst (2-4), senior analyst (4-7), lead/principal or analytics manager (6-10+), head of analytics/insights (10+). A UK path cited by Prospects: junior, analyst, senior, lead, analytics manager. Progression often needs a specialism (finance, product, risk) or management.

exits.label: Exit opportunities
exits.md: After 2-3 years: BI developer, analytics engineer, product/marketing analyst, data scientist (with more stats), business analyst/product owner, consulting. After 7-10 years: analytics manager/head of analytics, product manager, strategy and operations, finance business partner, chief-of-staff style roles, data governance lead.

tiers.label: Tier list of employers
tiers.md:
Tier groupings reflect industry consensus and practitioner perception, not objective fact.
- Tier 1 (pay, brand, data maturity): Big Tech and top scale-ups (Meta, Amazon, Google, Microsoft, Booking.com, Spotify, Uber), plus top-tier banks' central analytics groups and strategy/analytics consultancies. Strong tooling, high pay, competitive hiring, sometimes narrow scope.
- Tier 2: large corporates with mature analytics teams (retailers such as Walmart, Tesco, Zalando, FMCG such as Unilever, P&G, Nestle, telecoms, insurers, pharma), Big 4 data practices. Good training, structured graduate schemes, moderate pay.
- Tier 3: SMEs, agencies, public sector and outsourcers: more generalist, less tooling, lower pay, but broader exposure and faster responsibility.
(Italy: most analysts work in Tier 2/3 organisations; global Tier 1 employers hire in Milan only in small numbers.)

enter.label: How to enter
enter.md: Degrees: economics, statistics, maths, engineering, computer science, business with a quantitative bent; the Government Statistical Service wants a degree with at least 25% statistical content; Prospects says other degrees work if you show analytical skills. Routes: graduate schemes (UK: open September, close between November and January per TargetJobs), internships, UK Level 4 data analyst apprenticeships, the UK Government Analysis Function / Fast Stream (year-one spot rate £31,554, £34,078 with London allowance, 2025-26 award). Italy: tirocinio/stage into a contract, often via master's or university placement; hiring is rolling (general knowledge). Interview formats: SQL live or take-home test (joins, window functions, aggregation), Excel exercise, a mini case ("churn is up, what do you check?"), dashboard critique, behavioural interview. Certifications: PL-300 (Microsoft Power BI Data Analyst, about USD 165, pass mark 700; helps if the employer uses Power BI), Tableau Desktop Specialist, Google Data Analytics Certificate (learning value, little hiring weight; verify current status); none replaces a portfolio. Build: 2-3 projects on real messy data with SQL, a published dashboard, and a written recommendation; show you can define metrics. Mistakes: tool-collecting with no business story, tutorial-clone portfolios, ignoring SQL fundamentals, over-selling Python. Alternative routes: internal moves from finance, operations or customer service (often the easiest), bootcamps (mixed outcomes; unverified outcome data), career changers with domain expertise. Entry difficulty: 3/5.

downsides.label: Honest downsides and who it is NOT a good fit for
downsides.md: Routine reporting is the exposed part of the job; junior hiring is soft and AI makes the "SQL plus chart" skill less scarce. You may be the order-taker for stakeholders who already decided the answer. Data cleaning dominates. Pay in Italy and much of Europe is low relative to the US. Not for: people who want to build models all day (data science), people who dislike ambiguity and stakeholder requests, or those wanting pure engineering.

roles.title: BI developer / BI analyst

what.label: What you actually do
what.md: You build the dashboards and the data model behind them. In Power BI you design star-schema models (fact tables of events, dimension tables such as product, store, date), write DAX measures (formulas, e.g. year-to-date revenue), set row-level security, tune refresh and performance, publish apps and train users. In Tableau or Looker you do the equivalent (calculated fields, LookML). You also write SQL views and liaise with data engineers. Deliverables: a certified dashboard, a governed dataset, documentation, user training. The brief example: you rebuild the weekly sales dashboard in Power BI, write the DAX measures and explain to the regional director why returns are up 8%.

day.label: A typical day and week
day.md: Stakeholder requirement session; building or fixing a report; debugging a number that "doesn't match finance"; checking refresh failures; user support tickets; sprint ceremonies if the team is Agile. Release rhythm is fortnightly. Peaks: month-end, board reporting, platform migrations (for example Tableau to Power BI).

hours.label: Hours, stress and lifestyle
hours.md: 37-42 hours; peaks 45-50 at close or migrations. Stress 3/5: tight reporting deadlines and "the CEO's dashboard is wrong" moments. Hybrid common; consultancy BI roles travel to clients (rarely heavy); contractors exist in the UK.

profile.label: Human vs. quantitative profile
profile.md: People/communication: 3/5. Quantitative/technical: 3/5 (technical rather than mathematical: modelling, DAX/SQL). You need design sense and patience with users more than statistics.

pay.label: Compensation (approximate)
pay.md:
- UK: Power BI adverts median £55,000 (25th £41,250, 75th £72,500; 2,355 adverts, 6 months to 9 Oct 2026, ITJobsWatch); Tableau median £55,000 (25th £40,000, 75th £75,000; 649 adverts). Entry about £28,000-£35,000 (author estimate informed by Prospects data-analyst starting range); senior £65,000-£85,000 (advert 75th percentile).
- US: Robert Half BI analyst base ranges (2026 guide city pages): New York $94,185-$141,960; San Diego $84,870-$127,920; Baltimore $71,760-$108,160; Rochester NY $64,170-$96,720; Rockford IL $60,030-$90,480 (low end is early-career, high end experienced); senior BI analyst San Diego $110,393-$158,670.
- Italy: Payscale early-career BI analyst EUR 35,000 median, EUR 25,000-41,000 base (2026); average BI analyst EUR 37,500 (Payscale, internally inconsistent percentiles). Milan consultancies pay juniors EUR 26,000-32,000 (SDG Group junior business analyst listing).
- Asia: Tokyo Power BI/business analyst advert JPY 6.5-8.5m (Michael Page Japan); Singapore: no BI-specific reliable data found.

path.label: Career path
path.md: Junior BI analyst (0-2), BI developer (2-4), senior BI developer/BI architect (4-8), BI lead/manager or head of reporting (8+). Many move sideways into analytics engineering or into data architecture.

exits.label: Exit opportunities
exits.md: After 2-3 years: analytics engineer, data analyst with a domain focus, data engineer (if SQL/ETL strong), Power Platform/low-code developer, product owner. After 7-10 years: BI/analytics architect, head of BI, enterprise data architect, pre-sales/solutions consultant at a vendor (Microsoft partner, Salesforce, Google), or independent contractor.

tiers.label: Tier list of employers
tiers.md:
Tier groupings reflect industry consensus and practitioner perception, not objective fact.
- Tier 1: product-led tech firms and vendors with modern stacks (Microsoft, Salesforce/Tableau, Google/Looker, Databricks, Snowflake), and data-mature banks; best engineering practices and pay.
- Tier 2: large corporates and insurers with central BI teams, Big 4 and Accenture/Capgemini data practices; Microsoft-partner consultancies.
- Tier 3: SMEs, agencies, outsourced BI support teams, public sector; legacy tools (Excel and SSRS reports), thin governance, lower pay.

enter.label: How to enter
enter.md: Degrees: computing, information systems, business/engineering with SQL. Many BI developers start as reporting analysts or in finance/operations and move across. Programmes: Big 4/consulting analyst intakes, corporate IT graduate schemes, vendor-partner trainee programmes. Interview: SQL test, Power BI/Tableau task (build a dashboard from a supplied CSV in 60-90 minutes or take-home), data modelling questions (star schema, relationships, cardinality), DAX/calculation puzzle, dashboard critique. Certifications: PL-300 is the one that visibly appears in adverts (UK Power BI is the most cited tool); Tableau specialist certs; dbt or SQL certs optional. Skills: SQL first, then one BI tool deeply, dimensional modelling, performance tuning, storytelling. Portfolio: a public Power BI/Tableau Public report on messy data plus a model diagram. Mistakes: pretty dashboards on a bad model, no documentation, 40-chart "dashboards" nobody uses. Alternative routes: from Excel-heavy finance or operations roles (the most common), Level 4 UK apprenticeships, bootcamps with a real project. Entry difficulty: 3/5.

downsides.label: Honest downsides and who it is NOT a good fit for
downsides.md: Self-serve BI and Copilot reduce demand for basic dashboard building; you are vulnerable if you only build report pages. Tool-specific careers can date quickly. Lots of maintenance and "why does my number differ" support work. Not for: those who dislike repetitive precision, or who want to do advanced statistics.

roles.title: Analytics engineer

what.label: What you actually do
what.md: You own the transformation layer. In dbt you write SQL models, define tests (not-null, unique, accepted values), document columns, manage dependencies, build a semantic layer (central metric definitions) and optimise warehouse cost. You work in Git with code review and CI. You turn messy source tables into clean "marts" (e.g., a customers table with consistent definitions) that analysts and BI tools use. Tools: SQL, dbt, a warehouse (Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks), Git, orchestration (Airflow, dbt Cloud), light Python. Deliverables: tested models, data contracts, metric definitions, lineage docs.

day.label: A typical day and week
day.md: Pull request review; fix a failing test after an upstream schema change; a conversation with an analyst about a new metric; model refactor; monitoring warehouse costs; incident triage when a dashboard breaks. Weekly sprint planning. Less meeting-heavy than analysts, more pull requests.

hours.label: Hours, stress and lifestyle
hours.md: 38-42 hours; peaks 45-50 during migrations or incidents; occasional on-call-lite for data incidents. Stress 3/5. Remote-friendly; scale-ups often fully remote or hybrid.

profile.label: Human vs. quantitative profile
profile.md: People/communication: 2/5 (3 with stakeholders). Quantitative/technical: 4/5 (technical depth, SQL and engineering practice, rather than maths).

pay.label: Compensation (approximate)
pay.md:
- US: dbt Labs 2025 survey (North America individual contributors, fielded late 2024): over 80% earn over $100,000 (up from 69%); managers over $200,000: 49%. Hiring-guide estimates for 2026 vary: junior $75,000-$105,000, mid $105,000-$145,000, senior $145,000-$190,000 (secondary blogs; base vs total mixed).
- UK: dbt-citing adverts median £74,830 (25th £62,500, 75th £85,625; 306 adverts, 6 months to 9 Oct 2026; the median is down 32% year on year, probably a mix effect of fewer senior ads, ITJobsWatch). No reliable entry figure; analytics engineers are rarely hired as graduates; entry from analyst roles about £45,000-£55,000 (author estimate, unverified).
- Europe: dbt survey: 51% of European ICs earn over USD 50,000 (up from 40%), managers over USD 100,000: 51% (down from 79%); Berlin senior listings EUR 75,000-100,000 (stale ad, 2025). Italy: no analytics-engineer figures found; a junior data engineer in Italy is estimated at USD 37,900-51,900 (Jobicy, July 2026, low confidence).
- Asia: no reliable data found.

path.label: Career path
path.md: Often analyst (1-3 years) then analytics engineer (2-5), senior (5-8), staff/lead analytics engineer or analytics engineering manager (8+). Few true graduate entry points.

exits.label: Exit opportunities
exits.md: After 2-3 years: data engineer, senior analyst/product analyst with strong data skills, data platform roles. After 7-10 years: staff/principal analytics engineer, data engineering lead, head of data, solutions architect, vendor roles (dbt, Fivetran, Snowflake).

tiers.label: Tier list of employers
tiers.md:
Tier groupings reflect industry consensus and practitioner perception, not objective fact.
- Tier 1: data-mature tech and fintech (for example N26, Booking.com, Spotify-class firms, Monzo, Stripe-class firms) and vendors; strong peer groups, engineering culture.
- Tier 2: scale-ups, larger e-commerce/retail, consultancies with modern-data-stack practices (including Accenture, Deloitte).
- Tier 3: companies adopting dbt for the first time, small teams where you are the sole data person; broad but isolated.
In Italy such roles are concentrated in Milan scale-ups, consultancies and a few international firms; supply of roles is small (no postings found in this research).

enter.label: How to enter
enter.md: Backgrounds: computing, engineering, quantitative degrees, or analysts who learned dbt on the job. Programmes: almost none; join as a data analyst or junior data engineer and move; some consultancies hire juniors onto dbt projects. Interview: SQL (window functions, CTEs), data modelling, a take-home dbt project or live modelling task, code review of a bad model, system design for a metrics layer, Git basics. Certifications: dbt Analytics Engineering Certification exists (cost unverified here) and signals tool knowledge but is less decisive than a working repository; cloud warehouse certs (SnowPro, Google Cloud data) optional. Skills/portfolio: a public dbt project on open data with tests, docs, CI, and a clear README; contribute to dbt packages. Mistakes: learning dbt without strong SQL; ignoring testing; no stakeholder skills. Alternative routes: analyst-to-AE internal move; bootcamp graduates have little traction here (unverified). Entry difficulty: 4/5.

downsides.label: Honest downsides and who it is NOT a good fit for
downsides.md: Barely any junior roles; AI coding assistants speed up SQL generation, raising the bar for juniors. A thin career ladder in small firms. Tool dependence on a vendor ecosystem that is consolidating (dbt Labs and Fivetran). Not for: people who dislike engineering discipline (testing, Git, reviews), or who want primarily stakeholder-facing work.

roles.title: Marketing, digital and product analyst

what.label: What you actually do
what.md: You measure how customers behave and which actions pay back. Tasks: set up and QA tracking (Google Tag Manager, GA4, Adobe Analytics, app SDKs), build funnel and cohort reports, analyse campaign performance and channel attribution (last-click, multi-touch, marketing-mix modelling at the senior end), segment customers in the CRM, support A/B tests (power calculations, reading results), and build marketing or product dashboards (Looker Studio, Tableau, Power BI, Amplitude). Deliverables: weekly performance report, experiment readout, customer segmentation, a "why did sign-ups fall" investigation.

day.label: A typical day and week
day.md: Check tracking and campaign dashboards; a stand-up with performance marketers or a product squad; analyse a feature launch; QA a tag release; Friday summary. Peaks around launches, Black Friday and quarter planning. In product teams you sit in a squad with a PM and engineers.

hours.label: Hours, stress and lifestyle
hours.md: 38-43 hours; peaks 48-55 around launches and seasonal peaks. Stress 3/5: pressure for quick answers, fast-changing priorities, and noisy data (consent rules reduce tracked traffic). Hybrid/remote common in digital firms; agencies busier.

profile.label: Human vs. quantitative profile
profile.md: People/communication: 3/5. Quantitative/technical: 3/5. Statistics matters for testing (significance, sample size) but most work is clear metrics, SQL and storytelling.

pay.label: Compensation (approximate)
pay.md:
- US: BLS market research analysts median $78,760 (May 2025). Payscale: product analyst average $78,222 (range $58,000-$110,000), product marketing analyst $59,506 ($43,000-$76,000); Indeed US product analyst average base $106,219 (tech-weighted). Entry about $55,000-$75,000; senior product analysts at tech firms $130,000-$180,000+ (author estimate from Levels.fyi-type ranges, unverified).
- UK: digital analytics adverts median £41,750 (6 months to May 2025, only 18 salaries; ITJobsWatch, last available); recent ads: Digital Analyst Birmingham £40,000-£48,000; Senior Digital Product Analyst London (retail) £55,000-£65,000; Senior Digital Analyst up to £60,000 (job listings, 2026). Entry about £25,000-£32,000 (author estimate).
- Italy: no reliable data found; junior analytics in agencies/e-commerce plausibly EUR 24,000-30,000 (author estimate, unverified).
- Asia/Middle East: no reliable role-specific data found.

path.label: Career path
path.md: Junior analyst (0-2), analyst (2-4), senior/lead analyst (4-7), analytics manager/head of insights (7-10+). Product analysts may become product managers or data scientists.

exits.label: Exit opportunities
exits.md: After 2-3 years: data scientist (experimentation), product manager, growth marketing, CRM/lifecycle manager, BI developer. After 7-10 years: head of marketing analytics or growth, product director, consumer insights lead, consultant.

tiers.label: Tier list of employers
tiers.md:
Tier groupings reflect industry consensus and practitioner perception, not objective fact.
- Tier 1: large tech and marketplaces with in-house experimentation platforms (Meta, Amazon, Google, Booking.com, Uber, Spotify, Airbnb), major e-commerce.
- Tier 2: retailers, banks' digital teams, telecoms, FMCG, media groups, large analytics consultancies.
- Tier 3: agencies and small ecommerce: heavy reporting, high churn, lower pay.

enter.label: How to enter
enter.md: Degrees: marketing, economics, business, statistics, computing; marketing graduates with SQL stand out. Programmes: marketing and digital graduate schemes at FMCG/retail (rotation through insights), agency analyst roles, tech associate analyst programmes. Interviews: SQL test, case ("sign-ups dropped 15% week over week; walk me through"), metrics/product-sense questions, A/B test interpretation, GA4 familiarity. Certifications: Google Analytics certification (free, entry signal only), Google Data Analytics certificate (low hiring weight), Adobe Analytics, Amplitude academy; none substitute for SQL. Portfolio: GA4 demo-account analysis, an A/B test write-up, a funnel dashboard. Mistakes: reporting vanity metrics, ignoring consent/privacy limitations, confusing correlation with attribution. Alternative routes: from performance marketing or CRM roles into analytics; self-taught with SQL; agency start then in-house move. Entry difficulty: 3/5 (agencies 2, tech product analytics 4).

downsides.label: Honest downsides and who it is NOT a good fit for
downsides.md: Attribution is inherently uncertain and privacy rules (GDPR, cookie consent, browser restrictions) are eroding tracking; people often want numbers that justify a campaign already run. AI is automating campaign reporting; Stanford found marketing among the most exposed early-career occupations. Not for: people who want certainty, or want a model-heavy role.

roles.title: Operations and supply-chain analyst

what.label: What you actually do
what.md: You analyse physical flows. Tasks: demand forecast accuracy and baseline forecasting in Excel/SAP IBP/Python, inventory analysis (safety stock, ageing, ABC classification), supplier OTIF reports, transport cost and lane analysis, warehouse productivity, S&OP (sales and operations planning) packs, procurement spend analysis, and process mining. Tools: Excel (heavy), SQL, Power BI/Tableau, ERP data (SAP, Oracle), Python occasionally, planning systems (Kinaxis, o9, Blue Yonder). Deliverables: weekly service-level dashboard, inventory reduction proposal, root cause of late deliveries.

day.label: A typical day and week
day.md: Pull ERP data; reconcile; update a KPI pack; talk to planners and warehouse managers; investigate a stock-out; join the weekly S&OP; occasional site visit. Disruptions (port delays, supplier failures) trigger urgent analyses.

hours.label: Hours, stress and lifestyle
hours.md: 38-45 hours; peaks 50-55 at S&OP cycle, peak season (retail Q4) or disruption. Stress 3/5 (4 in crisis weeks). Often on-site or hybrid; some travel to plants and depots, more in consulting (BLS notes management analysts travel frequently).

profile.label: Human vs. quantitative profile
profile.md: People/communication: 3/5. Quantitative/technical: 3/5. You must understand the operation and persuade planners and managers who know it better than you.

pay.label: Compensation (approximate)
pay.md:
- US: BLS operations research analysts median $88,940 (10th $57,060, 90th $159,910; May 2025), logisticians median $82,320; ASCM 2026 report: median supply chain base $98,500, total $103,500 (all levels; 10th percentile base $60,000); Payscale entry-level supply chain analyst average $63,684 ($50,000-$78,000). Senior and analytics-heavy roles at big retailers $110,000+ (author estimate).
- UK: Payscale entry-level supply chain analyst £26,114 (range £22,000-£31,000, 2026, self-reported); demand planning analyst advert Edinburgh £35,000-£40,000 (July 2025). Mid and senior: no reliable 2026 data found (recruiter guides were paywalled).
- Italy: no reliable data found; manufacturing and FMCG supply-chain graduates typically start in the EUR 26,000-32,000 range (author estimate, unverified).
- Asia/Middle East: no reliable data found.

path.label: Career path
path.md: Analyst (0-2), senior analyst/planner (2-5), supply-chain manager or S&OP/demand planning manager (5-8), head of planning/analytics or director (10+). Certifications (CPIM/CSCP) assist progression.

exits.label: Exit opportunities
exits.md: After 2-3 years: demand/supply planner, procurement analyst, logistics consultant, process improvement, BI/analytics. After 7-10 years: supply chain manager/director, operations consulting, S&OP head, supply chain data/digital lead, vendor roles (planning software).

tiers.label: Tier list of employers
tiers.md:
Tier groupings reflect industry consensus and practitioner perception, not objective fact.
- Tier 1: global FMCG/retail/consumer and industrial leaders with strong supply-chain academies (for example Unilever, Procter & Gamble, Nestle, Amazon, Apple, Walmart), and strategy/operations consultancies.
- Tier 2: large manufacturers, automotive suppliers, pharma, third-party logistics (DHL, Maersk, Kuehne+Nagel), mature retailers.
- Tier 3: SMEs and local distributors: Excel-based, broad but low analytic depth.
(Italy: manufacturing and fashion/food firms around Milan, plus logistics operators, are the main employers.)

enter.label: How to enter
enter.md: Degrees: supply chain/logistics, engineering, business, economics, maths. Programmes: operations/supply-chain graduate schemes at FMCG, retail, manufacturers and 3PLs (UK intakes typically open September and close Nov-Jan; unverified for each firm); internships on site are valued. Interviews: Excel exercise (VLOOKUP/pivot, forecasting), case (reduce stock-outs without raising inventory), SQL basics, behavioural. Certifications: APICS/ASCM CPIM or CSCP help; ASCM reports certified professionals earn up to 20% higher median salary (association's own survey, so treat with care); Lean Six Sigma green belt is common; PL-300 for the analytics edge. Skills/portfolio: forecasting exercise, inventory simulation, dashboard on public logistics data. Mistakes: pure theory without an operations feel; ignoring data quality in ERP. Alternative routes: from planning/warehouse operations into analytics; from engineering. Entry difficulty: 2/5.

downsides.label: Honest downsides and who it is NOT a good fit for
downsides.md: Pay starts modest (UK entry about £26,000 by Payscale); work depends on messy ERP data and manual Excel; firefighting in disruptions; plants and warehouses are often away from city centres. AI and planning software automate baseline forecasting. Not for: people who want pure data work without operational context, or who dislike on-site presence.

roles.title: People/HR analyst

what.label: What you actually do
what.md: You turn HR data into reports and answers: headcount and attrition dashboards, hiring funnel and time-to-fill, pay equity analyses, engagement survey analysis, workforce planning. Tools: Excel, Workday/SAP SuccessFactors reporting, Power BI/Tableau (or Visier), SQL, sometimes R/Python for attrition models. Deliverables: monthly people dashboard, board workforce pack, compensation benchmarking.

day.label: A typical day and week
day.md: Extract HRIS data; reconcile headcount against finance; build or update a dashboard; meet HR business partners; handle ad hoc questions; protect privacy (aggregation thresholds). Peaks at annual reviews, pay rounds and survey cycles.

hours.label: Hours, stress and lifestyle
hours.md: 37-42 hours; peaks 45-50 in pay-review cycles. Stress 2/5. Predictable, hybrid-friendly, minimal travel.

profile.label: Human vs. quantitative profile
profile.md: People/communication: 4/5. Quantitative/technical: 3/5. Trust and discretion matter as much as skills.

pay.label: Compensation (approximate)
pay.md:
- US: BLS HR specialists median $75,940 and compensation, benefits and job-analysis specialists $78,210 (May 2025); HR analyst entry $55,000-$65,000, mid $70,000-$85,000, senior $90,000-$116,000 (hr.university, unsourced, weak); Coursera/Glassdoor average $66,282 (April 2025).
- Western Europe: people analytics EUR 45,000-65,000, up to EUR 55,000-80,000 with Python/R (Freenance, weak source).
- UK, Italy, Asia: no reliable data found.

path.label: Career path
path.md: HR analyst (0-3), senior HR analyst (3-6), people analytics manager (6-10), head of people analytics / HR insights (10+).

exits.label: Exit opportunities
exits.md: After 2-3 years: HR business partner, compensation analyst, HRIS analyst, general data analyst. After 7-10 years: head of people analytics, reward lead, HR transformation, workforce planning, consulting at HR/people-analytics advisors.

tiers.label: Tier list of employers
tiers.md:
Tier groupings reflect industry consensus and practitioner perception, not objective fact.
- Tier 1: very large multinationals with dedicated people-analytics teams (global banks, consumer and tech firms) and specialist vendors (Visier, Workday).
- Tier 2: large corporates and consultancies' HR practices (Mercer, WTW, Aon, Big 4 people advisory).
- Tier 3: mid-size firms where HR analytics is a part-time duty inside HR operations.

enter.label: How to enter
enter.md: Degrees: psychology/organisational behaviour, management with HR, economics, statistics. Programmes: HR graduate schemes with rotations; few analyst-specific. Interviews: Excel/dashboard exercise, HR scenario, attrition analysis case. Certifications: CIPD (UK), SHRM (US) helpful for HR credibility; Visier/Workday training; PL-300 optional. Skills: HR metrics, stats basics, discretion, GDPR/employee-data privacy. Portfolio: attrition analysis on public HR datasets. Mistakes: surveillance-style analysis, ignoring privacy and bias. Alternative: HR coordinator or HRIS role to analytics. Entry difficulty: 3/5 (few openings, small teams).

downsides.label: Honest downsides and who it is NOT a good fit for
downsides.md: Small field with few roles; data volumes are small so statistics is often thin; privacy, works-council (Europe) and ethics limits what you can do; HR budgets are cut in downturns. Not for: people who want large datasets, rapid career progression through technical skill, or high pay.

roles.title: Data governance, data quality and data steward roles

what.label: What you actually do
what.md: You make data trustworthy and compliant. Data stewards own the definition and quality of a data domain (customer, product, supplier): they write business glossaries, set quality rules, resolve issues, and approve changes. Governance analysts and leads maintain the data catalogue (Collibra, Alation, Microsoft Purview, Informatica), lineage, data classification, retention, access policies, privacy impact assessments, and support regulatory requirements (GDPR; BCBS 239 for banks; AI/data documentation for the EU AI Act). Data quality analysts profile data, build rules and dashboards, track defect rates and root causes. Deliverables: policy, glossary, quality scorecard, issue log, catalogue entries.

day.label: A typical day and week
day.md: Workshop with a business owner to define "active customer"; review a data-quality dashboard; chase a source-system owner to fix errors; update the catalogue; present to a data council; respond to an audit or privacy request. Meetings dominate.

hours.label: Hours, stress and lifestyle
hours.md: 36-42 hours; peaks 45-50 before regulatory deadlines or audits. Stress 2/5 (3 in banks under regulatory scrutiny). Hybrid common; minimal travel.

profile.label: Human vs. quantitative profile
profile.md: People/communication: 4/5. Quantitative/technical: 2/5. Success depends on persuading people to own data; light SQL and profiling skills suffice at entry.

pay.label: Compensation (approximate)
pay.md:
- UK: "Data Governance" adverts median £70,000 (25th £56,250, 75th £87,500, 90th £105,000; 1,488 adverts, 6 months to 9 Oct 2026, ITJobsWatch; advert pool skews experienced). Data Steward: 1 advert in the period, so unreliable; the 2024 equivalent was median £37,000 (25th £31,250, 75th £39,750; 18 adverts). Data Governance Lead advert £70,000-£75,000 (2026 listing). Entry (steward/analyst) about £30,000-£38,000 (derived from 2024 steward data).
- US: no reliable survey found; one unsourced aggregator suggests about $115,000 for governance specialists (treat as unverified). Entry about $60,000-$80,000 (author estimate).
- Italy: no reliable data found; roles are concentrated in banks, insurers and large corporates, Milan-heavy.
- Asia/Middle East: no reliable data found.

path.label: Career path
path.md: Data steward/quality analyst (0-3), governance analyst/specialist (2-5), governance lead or data quality manager (5-8), head of data governance / chief data office roles / Chief Data Officer (10+). Moves between governance, privacy and risk are common.

exits.label: Exit opportunities
exits.md: After 2-3 years: data analyst, privacy/compliance analyst, data product owner, risk data roles. After 7-10 years: Head of Data Governance, Chief Data Office director, data protection officer, data risk lead, consulting (data strategy, privacy advisory).

tiers.label: Tier list of employers
tiers.md:
Tier groupings reflect industry consensus and practitioner perception, not objective fact.
- Tier 1: global banks and insurers with large chief-data-office teams, regulated pharma, big consultancies' data governance practices, and governance vendors (Collibra, Alation, Informatica, Microsoft Purview).
- Tier 2: utilities, telecoms, public agencies, Big 4 risk and data practices.
- Tier 3: firms doing governance as a compliance chore with a small team; heavy documentation, little influence.

enter.label: How to enter
enter.md: Backgrounds: information management, business, law/compliance, accounting, data analytics, computing. Programmes: a few bank chief-data-office graduate rotations; otherwise enter via data analyst, risk, compliance, audit or master-data roles. Interviews: scenario ("a customer table has 12% missing postcodes; what do you do?"), basic SQL, knowledge of GDPR principles, stakeholder behavioural. Certifications: DAMA CDMP (Associate level based on a Data Management Fundamentals exam; Coursera lists fees of about $311 for Associate, $933 for Practitioner and $983 for Master, to verify on dama.org); UK adverts list it as "preferred", not required; privacy certs (CIPP/E, CIPM from IAPP) help in privacy-adjacent roles. Skills: SQL profiling, data modelling basics, catalogue tools, regulation literacy, workshop facilitation. Portfolio: a data quality assessment on an open dataset, a glossary and rules document. Mistakes: treating governance as policy-writing without business adoption. Alternative routes: from audit/compliance, finance data, or analysts who "own" a dataset. Entry difficulty: 3/5 (few true entry-level roles; internal moves common).

downsides.label: Honest downsides and who it is NOT a good fit for
downsides.md: Seen as a cost centre; success is invisible when it works and blamed when it fails; slow, political change. Tooling is crowded and vendor-driven. AI makes governance more important but also threatens parts of manual documentation. Not for: people wanting hands-on technical building or quick wins; those who dislike meetings and negotiation.
