roles.title: Sales and business development (SDR/BDR to account executive; key account manager)

what.label: What you actually do
what.md:
- *SDR/BDR (software):* find potential customers, send emails, call and message them, and book meetings for account executives. Example: 40-60 outbound touches a day, aiming for a handful of meetings a week (activity targets vary by company).
- *Account executive (AE):* run demos, negotiate, and close deals against an annual quota (target). Pipeline reviews every week.
- *Key account manager (FMCG):* manage a retailer relationship: negotiate promotions and listings, forecast volumes, handle conflicts, jointly plan with brand teams.
- *Luxury retail/clienteling and pharma sales (brief):* luxury sales advisors build lasting client relationships; pharma sales representatives (Italy: "informatore scientifico del farmaco") visit doctors; both are regulated or high-training roles.
Tools: CRM (Salesforce, HubSpot), sales engagement software, LinkedIn Sales Navigator, call recording, increasingly AI assistants.

day.label: A typical day and week
day.md: SDR: prospecting blocks, calls and sequences, CRM updates, daily activity reviews. AE: demos, proposal writing, follow-ups, internal approvals. KAM: retailer meetings, promotion planning, monthly performance reviews. Month-end and quarter-end are pressure peaks.

hours.label: Hours, stress and lifestyle
hours.md: Typical 40-50 hours; peaks 55-60 at quarter-end (BLS: many sales reps work more than 40 hours; quotas add stress; Prospects: sales hours are "generally long" with early starts and late finishes). Stress 4/5: pay depends on quota. Travel varies from none (inside sales) to heavy (field and key account). Hybrid common in SaaS.

profile.label: Human vs. quantitative profile
profile.md: People/communication: 5/5. Quantitative/technical: 2/5. Persuasion, resilience and discipline dominate; you need pipeline math and basic product knowledge, not advanced statistics.

pay.label: Compensation (approximate)
pay.md:
- Entry (SDR): US median SDR OTE $80K (about $55K base, $25K variable, 68:32 split), 60% of SDRs at quota (Bridge Group, February 2025, 351 B2B companies). A secondary source citing RepVue shows median base about $60K and OTE about $85K (unverified). UK sales executive basic £25,000-£28,000 (Prospects, September 2025). Italy: inside sales €25-35k with bonus 10-20%; field sales €30-35k; sales account €35-40k (Michael Page Italy 2026, <5 years); medical sales rep €30-40k with 15-20% bonus. Hong Kong BD manager HK$30-55k per month (Morgan McKinley 2026).
- ~5 years (AE/KAM): US median AE OTE $200K (up from $190K in 2024), median quota $960K (4.6 times OTE), 48% of reps hit quota, ramp time 6.2 months, average experience at hire 3.7 years (Bridge Group AE report, 23 June 2026, 158 companies). RepVue medians via a secondary source (unverified): SMB AE about $130K OTE, mid-market $175K, enterprise $265K. Italy key account manager €55-70k (5-10 years, bonus 10-20%); pharma key account manager €65-90k (bonus 15-20%). Singapore key account manager S$95k at 5-10 years; Hong Kong key account manager (sales) HK$35-50k per month.
- Senior: Italy national account manager €75-85k, sales director €85-100k (bonus 25-35%), commercial director over €95k; UK senior sales over £100k with commission (Prospects, September 2025); Singapore head of sales/BD director S$160-300k.
Commission structure (SaaS): about 50/50 base/variable for AEs; median commission about 11.5% of annual contract value at quota (Bridge Group 2024 AE report via secondary summary, not re-verified).

path.label: Career path
path.md: SDR (12-24 months; average SDR tenure 1.9 years) to AE (SMB) to mid-market/enterprise AE (3-6 years) to sales manager/director (6-10) to VP sales / chief revenue officer. SDR promotions are scarcer: promotions were 16% of SDR attrition in 2024, down from 34% in 2020 (Bridge Group 2025). FMCG: sales rep/assistant KAM to KAM to national account manager to commercial/sales director.

exits.label: Exit opportunities
exits.md: After 2-3 years: AE, customer success, product marketing, sales operations, recruitment, marketing. After 7-10 years: sales director, VP, founder, general manager, or partnership/strategy leadership.

tiers.label: Tier list of employers
tiers.md:
- Tier 1 (by brand and training): Salesforce, Oracle, SAP, Microsoft, Google Cloud, HubSpot-type scale-ups; FMCG commercial rotations at P&G, Unilever, Nestle; luxury maisons for clienteling.
- Tier 2: mid-size SaaS, staffing, telecom, medical device, B2B industrial.
- Tier 3: commission-heavy, high-churn, low-base start-ups and call-centre-style outbound shops.
Tier groupings reflect industry consensus and practitioner perception, not objective fact.

enter.label: How to enter
enter.md:
- Degrees: any; business, marketing or economics help, technical degrees for technical/scientific sales (BLS: technical/scientific reps typically need a bachelor's). Pharma sales often prefers life-science degrees.
- Entry: SaaS SDR programmes at large vendors; FMCG sales graduate schemes (also parts of Unilever UFLP and P&G tracks); retail management trainee programmes; UK Level 4/6 sales apprenticeships.
- Calendar: SDR hiring is rolling and frequent; FMCG schemes follow the autumn cycle.
- Assessments: role-plays, cold-call exercises, personality tests, a final manager interview.
- Certifications: Salesforce Administrator/Trailhead and HubSpot sales certificates are optional proof; few firms require them.
- Skills: resilience, written outreach, listening, CRM familiarity.
- Mistakes: ignoring commission plan details and quota realism; accepting a role with a low base and high quota.
- Alternative routes: customer support or retail to SDR; SDR to marketing or product marketing.
Entry difficulty: 2/5 for SDR/inside sales; 4/5 for FMCG graduate sales schemes and KAM jobs at top firms.

downsides.label: Honest downsides and who it is NOT a good fit for
downsides.md: Variable pay and rejection; a 48% attainment rate for AEs and 60% for SDRs means many people miss targets (Bridge Group); SDR roles are the most exposed to AI automation (AI SDRs were first measured at 1% of respondents in 2025, a trend to watch). Not for people who need stable income, dislike targets or cold outreach, or want little interpersonal conflict.

roles.title: Central bank economist (research and policy tracks)

what.label: What you actually do
what.md: On the research track, you write working papers (pre-publication drafts) on topics such as inflation, labour markets or bank lending, estimate models in Stata, R, Python or MATLAB, present at internal seminars and external conferences and try to publish in journals; the Fed Board states its economists present at conferences, publish in peer-reviewed journals and circulate working papers (Fed Board, October 2026). On the policy track, you maintain forecasting models (for example a nowcast, an estimate of today's GDP or inflation from the latest data) and write briefing notes for the policy committee (FOMC at the Fed, Governing Council at the ECB, MPC at the Bank of England). The ECB graduate economist works on analytical and policy work, improves analytical tools, prepares groundwork for policy decisions and communications and represents the ECB externally (ECB graduate page, 2026). Research assistants (RAs) at the Fed prepare data for memos, run literature searches, draft limited-complexity analytical memos and handle data requests (Fed RA page, October 2026). Supervisory economists review banks' risk models and stress tests.

day.label: A typical day and week
day.md: Illustrative composite, not a measured schedule. Monday: update the data pipeline and nowcast in R or Python; Tuesday: draft two pages for the governor's briefing; Wednesday: seminar where a colleague's working paper is critiqued; Thursday: coding the model or regressions; Friday: meeting with the policy division. In the weeks before a rate decision, forecast rounds and briefing deadlines tighten. Researchers have weeks of protected time for papers.

hours.label: Hours, stress and lifestyle
hours.md: Typical 40-50 hours, peak 55-60 around forecast rounds and policy meetings (author judgement from practitioner descriptions; no survey found). Stress 2/5 for research, 3/5 for policy or crisis periods. Flexibility is good: most central banks offer hybrid work, and travel is occasional (conferences, committee meetings). Fed DC jobs are in-person in Washington (Fed Board, October 2026).

profile.label: Human vs. quantitative profile
profile.md: People/communication: 3/5. Quantitative/technical: 4/5. Research economists spend most time alone on code and writing; policy economists must turn technical results into short memos for non-economists, so writing matters as much as modelling.

pay.label: Compensation (approximate)
pay.md: *US*: Fed Board does not publish role pay on the pages I read; its 2025 FR salary structure runs from FR-16 (USD 36,400-44,400) up to FR-31 (up to USD 295,200), with no mapping to RA or PhD-economist jobs on the page (Fed Board salary page, 2025). A 2026 San Francisco Fed (a regional Reserve Bank) listing shows USD 80,000 for an economic research associate (Built In listing, 2026, snippet-level); a university career page cites about USD 60,000 for Fed RAs from Glassdoor (undated, unverified). *Euro area*: ECB Economist Graduate Programme, band E/F step 1, EUR 4,982 net per month plus benefits (about EUR 59,800 net per year over 12 months; ECB page, 2026 cycle). *UK*: Bank of England graduate programme GBP 33,525 (Leeds, 2026 listing, TargetJobs) and GBP 36,500 in London/32,750 Leeds for 2025 (Prospects); the Economist stream salary was not separated; the Bank's PhD Research Programme was advertised at GBP 60,000 but was not recruiting for 2025/26 (BoE research careers page, snippet-level). *Italy*: Bank of Italy Esperto (graduate-level) starting pay is reported at EUR 50,126 gross per year (money.it, 18 December 2025; secondary and unverified; the official notice does not state pay). *Asia*: HKMA Graduate Economist, HK$ 49,000-50,000+ fixed monthly pay plus lump-sum on completion (HKMA vacancy and programme page, 2026; currency symbol shown as "$"). ~5 years and senior: no reliable data found for any central bank; Fed senior pay can reach the upper FR grades, but role mapping is not published.

path.label: Career path
path.md: RA/analyst (0-2 years, often leaving for a PhD) -> economist (PhD, year 0-5) -> senior economist (5-10) -> principal economist/adviser -> division head/director. At the ECB the graduate programme lasts two years with an option for a third (ECB page). Bank of Italy is a permanent civil-service-style career entered by competitive exam (concorso).

exits.label: Exit opportunities
exits.md: After 2-3 years (RA): PhD programmes (the Fed says over half of RAs enter graduate programmes, mainly economics or finance PhDs), government or consulting. After 7-10 years (economist): IMF/World Bank, bank chief-economist roles, academia, economic consulting, tech.

tiers.label: Tier list of employers
tiers.md: *Tier 1 (research-heavy, global policy influence)*: Federal Reserve Board and New York Fed, ECB, Bank of England, BIS. *Tier 2*: other Reserve Banks, Bank of Italy, Bundesbank, Banque de France, Bank of Japan, MAS, HKMA, Bank of Canada. *Tier 3*: smaller or emerging-market central banks and financial supervisors, where analytical depth, publishing culture and PhD intensity vary widely. Tier groupings reflect industry consensus and practitioner perception, not objective fact. Gulf central banks and sovereign entities: no reliable data found on entry routes or pay.

enter.label: How to enter
enter.md: *Degrees*: PhD for research economist (ECB graduate economist requires a master's plus PhD in economics completed in the window, EU nationality, C1 English; Fed economist requires a PhD or dissertation in progress); bachelor's or master's for RA/analyst (Fed RA: bachelor's or master's in economics, statistics, maths, finance, data science or similar, US citizenship required); master's for many policy-analyst roles. *Programmes and calendar*: Fed RA applications Aug 17-Oct 15 per the Fed page, interviews Oct-Nov and Feb-May, rolling offers, start in June/July, two-year term. ECB Economist Graduate Programme 2026: application closed 6 January 2026, up to four posts, two-year fixed term from 1 September, written exercise, presentation, interview; the generalist graduate programme (19 places in total) is a separate track for master's graduates (library research, ECB page). BIS Graduate Programme: contract up to 11 months, salary net of Swiss income tax, advertised in spring; PhD fellowship in late summer (BIS pages). HKMA Graduate Economist: two-year programme, postgraduate degree in economics, finance or similar, 2026 deadline 9 January 2026, essay (about 300 words), aptitude test, written test, interview. Bank of Italy: Esperto economics profile December 2025 notice, 45 places, master's at 105/110 or above in listed classes (LM-77, LM-56, LM-16, LM-52, LM-62), 8,307 applications (about 185 per place), 60-question preselection, top 500 to written, top 400 to oral including English; separate PhD research fellowships for economists (six fellows, 12 months renewable once, October 2025 call). *Interview formats*: technical presentation of research, written exercise, policy memo. *Skills*: econometrics (time series, panel, causal inference), Stata/R/Python/MATLAB, clear writing. *Common mistakes*: applying with a master's to PhD-only research seats; missing the narrow window; ignoring nationality rules (EU-only at ECB; US-citizen only at the Fed RA). *Alternative routes*: RA jobs at the Fed or central bank, then PhD; for Italians, a concorso is the route and grade floors are hard. Entry difficulty: 4/5 (RA/analyst) to 5/5 (research PhD seats at tier 1).

downsides.label: Honest downsides and who it is NOT a good fit for
downsides.md: Policy impact is often indirect; senior decisions are made by committees. Research seats are PhD-gated, and the best ones are scarce (ECB: four economist posts in 2026). Pay is below consulting and tech, and in Italy it is tied to public scales. Public-exam routes (Bank of Italy) filter on grades and test performance more than on skills. Not a good fit if you want fast pay growth, client-facing work, or are not willing to commit to years of technical writing.

roles.title: Economist at an international organisation (IMF/World Bank/OECD/development banks)

what.label: What you actually do
what.md: IMF country economists draft parts of Article IV reports, a yearly assessment of a member country's economy, and estimate fiscal, monetary and external-sector scenarios; the IMF Economist Program rotates PhDs through country surveillance and programmes, policy analysis and research for flagship publications (IMF EP page, October 2026). World Bank economists write country economic memoranda, evaluate project impact and advise governments on reforms. OECD economists draft country surveys and statistical series. Tools: Stata, R, Python, spreadsheets and macro models; deliverables are reports, briefing notes and missions where you meet ministry officials.

day.label: A typical day and week
day.md: Illustrative composite. Weeks at HQ: data work, drafting a chapter and internal review meetings; mission weeks (one to two weeks, several times a year) mean travel to the member country for meetings with the finance ministry and central bank. A deadline-heavy "report week" can run late.

hours.label: Hours, stress and lifestyle
hours.md: Typical 40-50 hours, peaks 55-60 during missions and report deadlines (author judgement). Stress 3/5. Travel is substantial for IMF/World Bank (several missions a year; the IMF programme specifically includes surveillance missions) and lower at the OECD. Remote/hybrid is common but HQ-based. IO staff often live abroad on expatriate benefits.

profile.label: Human vs. quantitative profile
profile.md: People/communication: 4/5. Quantitative/technical: 4/5. You must negotiate with ministry officials and convey politically sensitive messages, not only run models.

pay.label: Compensation (approximate)
pay.md: *IMF*: the most recent public salary table I could retrieve is dated 1 May 2017: entry-level PhD economists sit at grade A11 (USD 95,090-142,610), economists at A12-A13 (A12 USD 108,670-163,000; A13 USD 124,620-186,950); these are old and current pay is higher (IMF Annual Report Web Table 3.4, 2017; 2025 table not retrievable). IMF salaries are generally not subject to national income tax and carry an internal staff assessment; I could not confirm current detail (unverified, general knowledge). *World Bank*: net-of-tax scales; US headquarters, effective 1 July 2023: GF USD 101,700-189,000 (midpoint 145,300), GG USD 131,900-245,000 (midpoint 188,500), GH USD 177,600-330,000 (World Bank Group net salary scale, 2023). FY27 scales exist but the PDF was unreadable (World Bank FY27 scales, 2026). Economists enter around GF (YPP is GF-level). *OECD*: Young Associates EUR 3,886 per month exempt from French income tax, plus leaving allowance around EUR 21,000 (OECD YAP page via Wayback capture of 1 September 2026, library research); senior OECD economist pay: no reliable data found. *EU institutions*: AD5 basic EUR 6,152.64 per month from 1 July 2025 (Council doc 16220/25, library research); net about EUR 4,859 with no allowances and EUR 5,870 with expatriation allowance (AMLA worked example, a Frankfurt EU agency; Brussels may differ by a few per cent). *EIB*: graduate programme at the minimum of grade level 3; EUR 56,125 reported by a search snippet (unverified). Italy: Italian JPO (Junior Professional Officer, state-funded) pay is set by the host organisation: no reliable data found. ~5 years and senior: IMF grades A12-A13 (2017 bands above) for economists and A14+ for division chiefs.

path.label: Career path
path.md: Research analyst or intern (0-2 years) -> Economist (PhD entrant, IMF Economist Program, 3 years) -> Senior Economist (5-8) -> Division/unit chief or advisor (10-15) -> Director. World Bank YPP: graduate degree plus 2-6 years' experience, two-year programme with three 8-month rotations, then a role at least a further 5 years on completion (World Bank YPP page, October 2026, via library research).

exits.label: Exit opportunities
exits.md: After 2-3 years: PhD, ministries, central banks, consulting. After 7-10 years: senior posts in governments (finance ministry, central bank), regional banks, private-sector chief economist roles, academia.

tiers.label: Tier list of employers
tiers.md: *Tier 1*: IMF, World Bank, OECD (policy influence, high selectivity). *Tier 2*: regional development banks (EIB, EBRD, ADB, IDB, AfDB), BIS, specialised UN bodies (UNCTAD, UNDP economics units). *Tier 3*: smaller UN agencies, NGOs and consultancies working on IO projects. Tier groupings reflect industry consensus and practitioner perception, not objective fact.

enter.label: How to enter
enter.md: *Degrees*: PhD for IMF Economist Program (recent PhD or within one year of completing, member-country national, under 34 when joining, apply by 4 December 2026 for September 2027 start; three-year programme with two 18-month assignments); bachelor's for IMF Research Analyst Program (recent bachelor's, GPA at least 3.5/4.0, two-year contract in Washington, apply by 30 December 2026) and OECD Young Associates (bachelor's only, no master's or PhD allowed, OECD-member nationality, GPA 3.0/4.0, 8-12 participants a year, applications Nov-Dec); master's plus 2-6 years for World Bank YPP (2027 cohort window was 1-30 September 2026, which has closed; start September 2027). UN YPP: bachelor's accepted, age 32 or younger, but only nationals of listed countries; Italy was not on the 2026 list (careers.un.org, October 2026). Italians can use the state-funded JPO programme (45 Italian places in 2026, born 1 January 1995 or later, master's; deadline was 5 May 2026). *Interview formats*: IMF EP has a preliminary interview, paper submission with three references, panel interview and written assessment; offers in February. *Skills*: macro and public finance, econometrics, writing, languages. *Common mistakes*: assuming a master's can enter the Economist Program (it cannot); missing narrow annual windows; ignoring nationality rules. *Alternative routes*: IMF RAP, OECD internships (about EUR 1,000 per month), EU Blue Book traineeships, development-bank graduate programmes (EIB GRAD, under two years since graduation), national secondments. Entry difficulty: 5/5 (Economist Program, YPP; no published acceptance rates).

downsides.label: Honest downsides and who it is NOT a good fit for
downsides.md: Extremely selective with narrow windows and nationality gates; IO pay is high but the cost of living in Washington, Paris or Luxembourg takes a chunk; slow, consensus-based work; heavy travel; promotion is slow past mid-grades; UN hiring was down (external recruitment to geographical posts was only 104 in 2024, from the library report). Not a good fit if you dislike bureaucracy or cannot relocate.

roles.title: Government economist / official statistician

what.label: What you actually do
what.md: UK GES economists produce cost-benefit analysis for spending proposals, evaluate programmes, advise ministers on policy trade-offs and write the economic sections of business cases. US BLS/BEA statisticians produce the monthly jobs/CPI and national accounts data, with large-scale data processing, seasonal adjustment and revisions; CBO analysts model the budget impact of bills; Treasury economists work on tax and international policy. In Italy, ISTAT researchers and technologists build national statistics; MEF staff cover public finance and tax analysis. Tools are Excel, Stata/R, SQL, increasingly Python.

day.label: A typical day and week
day.md: Illustrative composite. Morning: refresh data, check outliers in a series; midday: team meeting on a ministerial request; afternoon: write a two-page options note; weekly submission for a minister's deadline. Statistical offices follow a rigid release calendar (publication day is fixed and errors are public).

hours.label: Hours, stress and lifestyle
hours.md: Typical 37-45 hours, peaks 50-55 for ministerial deadlines, budget rounds or release days (author judgement). Stress 2/5, rising to 3/5 in spending reviews. Stable, hybrid-friendly, low travel.

profile.label: Human vs. quantitative profile
profile.md: People/communication: 3/5. Quantitative/technical: 3/5. Policy economists must explain trade-offs to non-economists; official statisticians skew toward 4/5 quantitative.

pay.label: Compensation (approximate)
pay.md: *UK*: GES Assistant Economist GBP 34,123 per year (2026 listing, JobsGoPublic aggregator); GBP 31,500 for the 2025 scheme; the Civil Service Fast Stream starts at GBP 31,554 (Civil Service Careers, 2 October 2026, library research). After training GBP 45,000-55,000 (Planit, undated, indicative). Grade 7 national minimum GBP 52,120 or 56,375 depending on the Defra snapshot; a commentary places Treasury/Cabinet Office G7 roles at the higher end of GBP 55,000-75,000 (secondary, unverified). *US*: BLS median for all economists USD 124,720 (May 2025); federal government median USD 144,680; state government USD 78,080; consulting USD 141,010 (BLS OOH, 2026). GS-9 (a typical master's entry grade) in Washington, DC 2026: about USD 70,623 step 1; GS-11 USD 85,447 step 1, USD 111,087 step 10; GS-12 USD 102,415-133,142 (OPM 2026 DC table via third-party reproduction; CBO uses its own scale, not checked). *Italy*: Bank of Italy Esperto about EUR 50,126 gross (secondary, unverified); MEF and ISTAT pay: no reliable data found. *EU*: AD5 about EUR 4,859-5,870 net per month (above).

path.label: Career path
path.md: GES: Assistant Economist (0-3 years, promoted to Economic Adviser within about 3 years per a 2022-23 GES outreach deck, salary GBP 45k+ ) -> Grade 7 Senior Economic Adviser (5-8 years) -> Grade 6 Deputy Director (10+). US: GS-7/9 economist -> GS-11/12 (3-5 years) -> GS-13/14 supervisory. Italy: permanent civil servant by concorso, progression by seniority and further exams.

exits.label: Exit opportunities
exits.md: After 2-3 years: PhD, regulator, consulting, central bank. After 7-10 years: consulting, think tanks, international organisations, bank economist roles, senior civil service.

tiers.label: Tier list of employers
tiers.md: *Tier 1*: HM Treasury, US Treasury, CBO, EU DG ECFIN and similar central policy shops that publish influential numbers. *Tier 2*: spending departments (UK Defra, DfT, DWP), BLS and BEA, ISTAT, MEF, national ministries. *Tier 3*: local-government and state-level units, where scope and pay are narrower (BLS: state government median USD 78,080, local USD 100,370, 2025). Tier groupings reflect industry consensus and practitioner perception, not objective fact.

enter.label: How to enter
enter.md: *Degrees*: UK GES requires a first or 2:1 in economics, a joint degree with at least half economics, or a postgraduate economics degree; micro and macro required; no visa sponsorship; Civil Service nationality rules apply; 50 hours a year of economics CPD (continuing professional development) plus 50 hours of personal skills (gov.uk, 2026). The 2026 window was 3-27 February 2026; the next round is likely early 2027 (gov.uk, closed page). US federal: bachelor's possible at GS-5/7, master's typical at GS-9; USAJOBS and the Pathways programme; citizenship usually required. Italy: concorsi via the InPA portal (a state recruitment platform with SPID identity); ISTAT's 2026 call offered 54 researcher and 46 technologist posts plus 95 technical collaborators (closed 22-23 January 2026; sources disagree: one outlet reports 100 posts), EU/Italian citizenship required; MEF's concorso closed 27 January 2026 with 485 funzionari posts (secondary, unverified) and a 40-question, 60-minute multiple-choice test. EU: EPSO competitions; the generalist AD5 competition EPSO/AD/427/26 drew 174,727 applicants for 1,490 places, 45% of them Italian, with reasoning tests from November 2026 (EPSO via library research); DG ECFIN economists are typically recruited through EPSO specialist competitions (unverified). *Interview formats*: online tests (numerical, verbal, situational), written exercises, panel interviews; Italian concorsi use written exams, preselection and orals. *Skills*: cost-benefit analysis, Excel, Stata/R, writing short briefs. *Common mistakes*: missing the nationality rules; applying to the UK Fast Stream as an EU graduate without settled status (not possible without right to work). *Alternative routes*: statistical offices as a back door (data skills valued), contract-agent database (CAST) for EU institutions, graduate internships. Entry difficulty: 3/5 (UK/US), 4/5 for oversubscribed EU and Italian competitions.

downsides.label: Honest downsides and who it is NOT a good fit for
downsides.md: Pay growth is slow; entry in Italy and the EU is a lottery-like exam with huge applicant pools; political direction constrains your conclusions; US federal roles are exposed to budget and hiring-freeze cycles (general observation, not sourced). Not a good fit if you want rapid pay or autonomy over research questions.

roles.title: Economic consultant (competition, litigation, regulation)

what.label: What you actually do
what.md: You build the empirical analysis behind an expert witness's report. In competition cases you estimate whether a merger would raise prices (using *merger simulation*, a model of how rivals react after a merger) or whether a cartel caused overcharges; in litigation you calculate damages; in regulation you analyse costs and returns of utilities. CRA's analyst posting lists researching economic and industry issues, building valuation models, running regressions in Excel, Stata, R, Python or SQL, summarising reports, depositions and academic literature, and quality-checking expert reports, tables and charts (CRA posting, 2026). Juniors do data cleaning and coding; PhD associates design the econometric strategy and draft expert reports.

day.label: A typical day and week
day.md: Illustrative composite. Monday: clean a dataset of transactions received from the client's lawyers; Tuesday-Wednesday: run regressions and sensitivity checks; Thursday: summarise findings in a slide deck for the case team; Friday: review a draft expert report. The weeks before a filing deadline or hearing are intense, with weekend work.

hours.label: Hours, stress and lifestyle
hours.md: Typical 45-55 hours, peak 65-80 before filings or trials (library research reports 45-60 hours with spikes to 75, unverified practitioner figure). Stress 4/5: client and legal deadlines drive crunch. Travel is moderate (client sites, depositions). CRA expects 3-4 office days a week (CRA posting, 2026).

profile.label: Human vs. quantitative profile
profile.md: People/communication: 3/5. Quantitative/technical: 4/5. Strong coding and clear writing for lawyers; client interaction grows with seniority.

pay.label: Compensation (approximate)
pay.md: *US analyst (bachelor's/master's), base*: CRA USD 92,500-100,000 (2027 graduates, posted 2026); Analysis Group Analyst USD 95,000-100,000 (Analysis Group pay page via search summary, undated); Cornerstone Research Analyst USD 112,500 base plus starting bonus (University of Florida career hub listing, recruiting from August 2026). *US PhD hires*: NERA Consultant (new PhD) USD 220,000-235,000 base (Built In posting, undated); Analysis Group Associate USD 180,000-240,000; Cornerstone Associate (Menlo Park) USD 195,000-245,000 (May 2026 posting). Glassdoor-based guide: median total pay for US economic consultants about USD 170,000 (2026, all levels, aggregator). *UK/Europe*: analyst GBP 48,000-62,000 plus 10-25% bonus; senior analyst GBP 65,000-80,000; PhD associate GBP 85,000-110,000 (library research; secondary and unverified - Frontier, Oxera and RBB do not publish salaries on the pages I found; Frontier lists pay as "competitive"). *Italy*: no reliable data found. *Asia/Gulf*: no reliable data found.

path.label: Career path
path.md: Analyst/research analyst (0-3 years, often a two- to three-year programme) -> Senior Analyst or Associate (PhD entrants start here) -> Manager/Senior Consultant (4-7 years) -> Vice President/Principal -> Partner/Affiliate expert (10+ years, usually a PhD and academic profile). Partner pay is uncapped and tied to origination of cases; data not available.

exits.label: Exit opportunities
exits.md: After 2-3 years: top economics PhD programmes (a major route), competition authorities (UK CMA, DG COMP), law, corporate strategy. After 7-10 years: big-tech antitrust and regulatory teams, regulators, hedge funds, academia.

tiers.label: Tier list of employers
tiers.md: *Tier 1*: the global pure-plays often cited by practitioners: Compass Lexecon, CRA, Cornerstone Research, Analysis Group, NERA, Brattle. *Tier 2*: European/UK specialists: Oxera, Frontier Economics, RBB Economics, CEPA; big-four and mid-sized practices (economic modelling and valuation). *Tier 3*: smaller boutiques and in-house economics units at law firms. Differences: tier 1 get the big antitrust and class-action cases and have academic affiliates; European firms lean to regulation and policy. Tier groupings reflect industry consensus and practitioner perception, not objective fact.

enter.label: How to enter
enter.md: *Degrees*: bachelor's or master's for analyst (CRA recruits December 2026 or summer 2027 graduates with a quantitative degree; honours thesis or research apprenticeship highly desired); PhD for associate. In Europe, a master's with strong econometrics (MSc/MPhil in Economics from a research-intensive university) is the standard credential; MBA or MiM without graduate econometrics are screened out (library research, unverified). *Calendar*: US analyst recruiting runs August-autumn for the following summer (CRA review from 17 August 2026, rolling; Cornerstone began 3 August 2026); PhD hires recruit around the AEA job market in January. *Interview formats*: resume screen, technical econometrics questions, a case or written test with data, behavioural interviews. *Skills*: Stata/R/Python/SQL, applied micro and industrial organisation (IO, the study of competition among firms), writing for lawyers. *Common mistakes*: generic consulting prep instead of econometrics prep; no coding sample or thesis; late applications. *Alternative routes*: research assistantships with professors, statistical office or regulator internships, master's thesis with data work. Entry difficulty: 4/5 (analyst at tier 1 firms), 4/5 for PhD associate (competitive).

downsides.label: Honest downsides and who it is NOT a good fit for
downsides.md: Billable-hour pressure and crunch before filings; the work is advocacy-adjacent (analysis is tailored to the client's side); junior work can be repetitive data cleaning; pay for analysts is lower than banking. Not a good fit if you dislike deadlines, working for a side, or want to do academic-style open research.

compare.name: Economic consultant

roles.title: Tech-sector economist

what.label: What you actually do
what.md: Design and test pricing, incentives and marketplace rules; estimate demand with *structural models* (models derived from economic theory) and causal effects from experiments (A/B tests) and observational data. Amazon listings describe causal inference for product selection, cost-to-serve and delivery speed, structural demand models for Prime Video investments, incrementality measurement for ads and labour-market analysis (Amazon.jobs, 2026). Uber's economists design pricing, incentives and subscription structures, run marketplace experiments and ML-driven optimisation; its policy-economics applied scientist role covers driver and courier policy (Uber postings, 2024-26). Airbnb's senior policy economists support regulation, housing, tourism and tax analysis (Airbnb posting, 2026). You write code in Python/R/SQL and present to product managers.

day.label: A typical day and week
day.md: Illustrative composite. Review overnight experiment results; refine an estimator; two meetings with product managers; write a one-page memo with a recommendation; weekly team read-out with engineers and data scientists.

hours.label: Hours, stress and lifestyle
hours.md: Typical 40-50 hours, peaks 55-60 around launches and quarterly planning (author judgement). Stress 3/5. Flexible, usually hybrid; limited travel. Layoff and reorganisation risk is real in tech (general observation, not sourced).

profile.label: Human vs. quantitative profile
profile.md: People/communication: 4/5. Quantitative/technical: 5/5. You must sell a model to product managers and engineers, and coding is expected.

pay.label: Compensation (approximate)
pay.md: *US (Amazon, Levels.fyi, updated 9 October 2026, 16 submissions)*: L4 median total compensation about USD 211,921; L5 about USD 295,812; overall median pay mix USD 147,000 base, USD 56,000 stock, USD 44,750 bonus. A snapshot of 11 August 2026 gave L4 USD 218,600, L5 USD 295,800 (the two vary, small sample). *Uber*: policy-economics applied scientist base USD 131,000-138,000 in San Francisco (Uber posting, undated). *Airbnb*: Senior Policy Economist USD 179,000-210,000; staff-level USD 194,000-240,000 (aggregator listings, approximate). INOMICS found the PhD premium among economists was 96% in 2023 (and about 50% in 2022) (INOMICS Salary Report). UK/Europe: no reliable data found. Asia: no reliable data found.

path.label: Career path
path.md: Economist/Scientist (PhD entry, L4) -> Senior Economist (L5, about 3-5 years) -> Principal/Tech Lead (L6, 8-12 years) -> Director/Chief Economist. Levels vary by company.

exits.label: Exit opportunities
exits.md: After 2-3 years: other tech, consulting, central banks, tenure-track academia. After 7-10 years: chief economist, product/strategy leadership, startup founding, antitrust expert roles.

tiers.label: Tier list of employers
tiers.md: *Tier 1*: Amazon (the largest economist team), Uber, Airbnb, Microsoft, Meta, Google, Netflix - perception based on size of economist teams and publication culture. *Tier 2*: Lyft, Spotify, eBay, Etsy, Booking, Zalando, fintechs. *Tier 3*: startups with one economist. Tier groupings reflect industry consensus and practitioner perception, not objective fact.

enter.label: How to enter
enter.md: *Degrees*: PhD (economics or similar) is the main route; Amazon lists a PhD in economics or equivalent as basic qualification for its marketing economists; Uber's marketing applied scientist role accepts PhD, MS or bachelor's with years of industry experience; Airbnb counts a PhD as roughly two years' experience for its senior role. *Calendar*: PhD candidates apply through the AEA job market (Uber's "AEA/ASSA economists" postings), fall-winter, with interviews in January; experienced hires apply all year. *Interview formats*: job-talk-style presentation of your research, coding screen (SQL/Python), causal-inference and experimentation questions, behavioural interviews. *Skills*: causal inference, experimentation, structural estimation, Python/SQL, ability to communicate to non-economists. *Common mistakes*: pure-theory PhD with no applied data skills; weak coding. *Alternative routes*: master's plus industry data science, then move into economist track (rare and role-dependent), pre-doc plus PhD. Entry difficulty: 5/5 (PhD from a strong programme practically required for the best seats).

downsides.label: Honest downsides and who it is NOT a good fit for
downsides.md: Many tech economists are used as senior data scientists; impact depends on product priorities; publishing is constrained. Compensation depends heavily on stock, which moves with the share price. Not a good fit if you want policy influence or academic freedom.

roles.title: Think-tank / policy researcher

what.label: What you actually do
what.md: Write policy briefs and papers, build data analysis for reports, present at events and brief journalists or officials. At the Resolution Foundation or IFS, analysts model tax and benefit changes and publish distribution analyses; at Bruegel, research assistants support economists on energy, climate or macro with data and drafting (job postings 2025-26).

day.label: A typical day and week
day.md: Illustrative composite. Morning: refresh data on household incomes; midday: draft a chart pack and two-page note; afternoon: meeting about a media briefing; end of week: proof a report before launch.

hours.label: Hours, stress and lifestyle
hours.md: Typical 40-50 hours, peaks 50-60 around budget days and publication launches (author judgement). Stress 3/5 due to short news cycles. Hybrid, limited travel except conferences.

profile.label: Human vs. quantitative profile
profile.md: People/communication: 4/5. Quantitative/technical: 3/5. Writing for non-specialists and handling media matter as much as statistics.

pay.label: Compensation (approximate)
pay.md: *UK*: Resolution Foundation (London), April 2026: Economist/Research and Policy Analyst GBP 45,170-56,990; Senior Economist GBP 56,990-70,300; Principal GBP 70,300-82,900. IFS Research Economist (doctorate required), September 2026 start: GBP 65,600; Senior Research Economist GBP 73,400-90,900 (IFS advert via search summary, 2026). Older IFS advert: new graduates about GBP 40,000 (undated). *US*: Brookings Economic Studies research assistant USD 58,000, two-year appointment, about 20 RAs a year, unionised (Brookings posting, 2026); PIIE research analyst USD 63,000-66,000 (PIIE posting, undated). *Brussels*: Bruegel research assistant one-year renewable contract, master's required, pay not stated; a third-party guide gives EUR 2,200-2,800 gross per month (unverified). New Economics Foundation Brussels economist EUR 47,946 (year unclear). *Italy*: no reliable think-tank pay data found. *Asia/Gulf*: no reliable data found.

path.label: Career path
path.md: Research assistant/analyst (0-2 years) -> Economist/Research fellow (3-5) -> Senior/Principal (5-8) -> Director/Fellow. Many leave to PhDs or government.

exits.label: Exit opportunities
exits.md: After 2-3 years: PhD, government, consulting. After 7-10 years: senior civil service, international organisations, politics/advisory, media, academia.

tiers.label: Tier list of employers
tiers.md: *Tier 1*: Brookings, PIIE, Resolution Foundation, IFS, Bruegel, CEPR. *Tier 2*: CEPS, Centre for European Reform, NEF, CER, sector think tanks. *Tier 3*: advocacy-driven or small organisations with limited research funding. Italian think tanks: I could not verify a roster; no reliable data. Tier groupings reflect industry consensus and practitioner perception, not objective fact.

enter.label: How to enter
enter.md: *Degrees*: master's for RA at Bruegel; bachelor's or master's at Brookings; doctorate for IFS research economist; PhD for Bruegel economist (2025 posting). *Calendar*: rolling, advertised on organisation websites and INOMICS. *Interview formats*: writing sample, data exercise, interview. *Skills*: Stata/R, charts, concise writing. *Common mistakes*: academic writing style, no portfolio. *Alternative routes*: internships, RAs, government analyst posts. Entry difficulty: 3/5.

downsides.label: Honest downsides and who it is NOT a good fit for
downsides.md: Low pay and fixed-term contracts (Bruegel postings: one-year renewable); funding dependence on donors; limited progression ladders. Not a good fit if you need financial stability early.

roles.title: Academic economist and pre-doctoral research assistant

what.label: What you actually do
what.md: *Academic economist*: research (write and publish papers), teach, supervise students, referee papers and apply for grants. *Pre-doc*: a research assistant who cleans data, runs regressions in Stata/R/Python, reads literature and sometimes co-authors; the work is a one- to two-year apprenticeship before a PhD application.

day.label: A typical day and week
day.md: Faculty (illustrative composite): two days of teaching/office hours, two days of research, seminar on one afternoon, refereeing and admin. Pre-doc: coding for the principal investigator, weekly meeting, reading papers.

hours.label: Hours, stress and lifestyle
hours.md: Faculty 45-60 hours with flexible scheduling; peaks at job-market season, grant deadlines and tenure review. Stress 3/5 for pre-docs; 4/5 for the PhD job market and tenure track (author judgement; EJMR-style anecdotes not used). Travel: conferences. Pre-docs 40-50 hours.

profile.label: Human vs. quantitative profile
profile.md: People/communication: 3/5. Quantitative/technical: 5/5. Research requires technical depth and writing; teaching and collaboration require communication.

pay.label: Compensation (approximate)
pay.md: *Faculty*: AEA Universal Academic Questionnaire reports average starting salary for assistant professors at PhD-granting institutions at USD 154,288 in 2024-25; another table shows USD 157,017 (AEA Papers and Proceedings 2025, 115:724-727; the two figures differ and the basis, nine- vs twelve-month, is unclear). Payscale's generic estimate is lower (about USD 74,863, not comparable). *Pre-docs (2026 postings)*: Harvard (Stantcheva) USD 50,000-55,000; USC USD 42,436 plus benefits; London Business School GBP 43,250, up to two years; LSE STICERD GBP 36,513-41,565 (rising to 44,468); an older Harvard/Yale/HBS fellowship offered USD 66,000. *PhD stipends*: Italian borsa about EUR 18,433 gross in 2026/27 at Brescia (university board decision, March 2026); Bocconi PhD EUR 27,000 year 1, EUR 23,000 later (library research); UKRI GBP 21,805 from 1 October 2026 (library research); LBS GBP 32,154 tax-free (library research). Italy faculty pay: no reliable data found. Asia/Gulf faculty pay: no reliable data found.

path.label: Career path
path.md: Pre-doc (1-2 years) -> PhD (US 5-6 years; Europe 3-5; library notes Bocconi 4 years) -> Assistant professor (tenure track, 6-7 years to tenure; US) -> Associate professor with tenure -> Full professor. In the UK, lecturer -> senior lecturer -> reader/professor. Italy: PhD -> postdoc/RTD-A/RTD-B -> associate professor via national qualification and local competition (system details: unverified in my sources).

exits.label: Exit opportunities
exits.md: After a PhD or 2-3 years on the market: industry (tech, consulting), central banks, IOs. ProMarket analysis: around two-thirds of PhDs took academic jobs in 2009, now roughly half, while tech rose from 1% of placements in the 2010s to 12% in the 2020s (ProMarket, accessed October 2026). After tenure: policy roles, central banks, consulting affiliate work.

tiers.label: Tier list of employers
tiers.md: Departments are conventionally ranked by research output (practitioner perception): *Tier 1*: MIT, Harvard, Chicago, Princeton, Stanford, Yale, Berkeley, LSE, Oxford, TSE, PSE and similar. *Tier 2*: other top-50 research universities. *Tier 3*: teaching-oriented colleges and universities. Pre-doc tiers: Fed/NBER/Harvard/Chicago-affiliated programmes versus smaller departments. Tier groupings reflect industry consensus and practitioner perception, not objective fact.

enter.label: How to enter
enter.md: *Degrees*: PhD required for faculty; bachelor's or master's for pre-docs (Fed RA, IMF RAP, think-tank RA also count as pre-doc-like). *Calendar of the academic job market (typical practice; AEA says interviews will occur online in 2026)*: candidate profiles and listings on JOE (Job Openings for Economists, the AEA's listings site) open in the late summer; applications are due in the autumn; first-round interviews historically ran at the January ASSA meetings (now online), followed by campus visits ("flyouts") in January-March and offers in spring. Hiring conditions: JOE listings in the second half of 2024 were down 4.6% from 2023 and 22.8% from 2022; the first half of 2025 was down 14.4% from 2024 and 39% from 2023 (AEA Committee on the Job Market, July 2025). The December 2025 department-chair survey attributed weakness to US university shocks (endowment tax, grant cuts, indirect-cost reductions, visa restrictions); I could not read the hiring count from the PDF. *Interview formats*: job market paper presentation (job talk), research conversations with faculty, teaching statement. *Skills*: econometrics, one's subfield, coding, writing. *Common mistakes*: starting a PhD without research experience or pre-doc; weak letters; no job market paper. *Alternative routes*: pre-docs (Harvard, USC, LBS, LSE and others; NBER predoc job announcement 2026), master's with thesis, central bank RAs. I found no systematic placement rate for pre-docs. Entry difficulty: 5/5 for top-programme tenure-track seats; 3/5 for pre-docs.

downsides.label: Honest downsides and who it is NOT a good fit for
downsides.md: 5-6+ years of stipend-level pay; a weak 2025-26 job market (listings down 39% vs 2023 by mid-2025); US-visa uncertainty; tenure review stress; pre-docs are low-paid and temporary. Not a good fit if you need income soon, dislike open-ended research, or want applied impact quickly.

roles.title: Strategy consultant (MBB and tier-2), analyst/associate to partner

what.label: What you actually do
what.md: You answer a business question in a few weeks. A typical project: a consumer-goods client asks whether to enter a new country. You build a market-sizing model in Excel, run 10-15 interviews with industry experts and customers, benchmark competitors, pull data from client systems and paid databases, and draft the steering-committee deck (often 20-40 slides) that your manager rewrites with you. Tools: Excel (heavily), PowerPoint (very heavily), Alteryx or Python at some firms, internal knowledge databases, and now firm AI tools (McKinsey's Lilli, BCG's GENE/Deckster) to summarise documents and draft slides. Deliverables: a model, a storyline, a final recommendation, sometimes an implementation roadmap. At MBB you are often "staffed" on your own module within the case, presenting results to the client within weeks.

day.label: A typical day and week
day.md: Hours 8-9 am: team check-in; morning: refine one analysis; midday: expert call or client working session; afternoon: build slides; late afternoon: problem-solving session with your manager ("what does this say?"); evening: finish the draft for the partner. In the traditional US/UK model the week is Monday to Thursday at the client's site and Friday in the home office; the travel day (usually Thursday evening) is a de facto lost evening. Post-2020 many teams are hybrid and total hours have not fallen much (StrategyCase, updated July 2026; a coaching site). Roland Berger states that consultants usually spend four days on-site and Friday in the office, with over 75% of its work cross-border (Roland Berger FAQ, 2026).

hours.label: Hours, stress and lifestyle
hours.md:
- *Hours:* typical 55-70 per week at MBB; peaks of 75-85 before key client meetings or in due-diligence sprints (StrategyCase, July 2026; PrepLounge coaching forum answers, 2025; no firm discloses hours; an old BCG study of North American staff found 92% worked 50+ hours and the average week fell from 64.5 to 57.7 hours after "predictable time off" rules, HBR/Wharton, 2009-12, stale). UK ONS paid-hours data shows only 38 hours because salaried overtime is unpaid, so ignore it as evidence on hours (earlier project research).
- *Stress:* **4/5.** Frequent high-stakes client pressure, constant evaluation, and an up-or-out ladder.
- *Lifestyle/flexibility:* low control over schedule between projects; partner and client demands dominate; first project assignment is mostly out of your hands. Parental leave and part-time policies exist at MBB but are used by a minority.
- *Travel:* high in the US and UK (weekly flights), often cross-border within Europe; Gulf and Asia teams often fly in for the week or are based locally. Hybrid has softened but not removed the four-day on-site norm.
- *Remote/hybrid:* partial; most client work involves some on-site days.

profile.label: Human vs. quantitative profile
profile.md: People/communication: 4/5. Quantitative/technical: 3/5. You need to be good with spreadsheets and structured problem-solving, but the differentiator is communicating a clear answer to senior people under time pressure; advanced maths is rare outside specialised teams.

pay.label: Compensation (approximate)
pay.md:
Entry (undergraduate/non-MBA master's):
- *US:* MBB base $110-112k (BCG $110k; McKinsey and Bain $112k) for 2025 offers; total cash with maximum bonus and signing about $137-140k (Management Consulted via Poets&Quants for Undergrads, Jan 2026). PrepLounge's US guide gives about $130-134.5k total (Jan 2026).
- *UK:* McKinsey £50,000 base (up to ~£60k total), BCG £49,500 (up to £60k), Bain £52,000 (up to £63k) (PrepLounge UK, updated 2026). Levels.fyi self-reports London McKinsey Business Analyst base about £55.3k (30 Sept 2026; self-reported). The two upstream data sets may overlap.
- *Germany/DACH (comparison):* McKinsey about €80k base, BCG and Bain about €75k (PrepLounge DACH, Dec 2025); a master's earns a higher entry grade than a bachelor's at McKinsey Germany (e-fellows.net McKinsey FAQ, 2026).
- *Italy:* **no reliable data found** for MBB or tier-2 graduate pay in Milan or Rome. Only scattered points: Oliver Wyman Italy about €43k base for undergraduate/master's level (Management Consulted 2026, single source, as noted in earlier research); a levels.fyi Milan listing showing Bain at an average of about €100k total across all levels (not entry). One PrepLounge forum user says Zurich pays "almost double" Milan (Aug 2025, anecdotal).
- *Middle East:* Dubai: McKinsey Business Analyst AED 255k base / AED 276k total, tax-free (levels.fyi, updated Sept 2026; self-reported); a coach estimates AED 20-30k per month for entry (PrepLounge forum, anecdotal). Riyadh: only post-MBA data found (BCG $304k, Bain $266k, McKinsey $242k total; PrepLounge Saudi 2025).
- *Asia:* Singapore MBB fresh graduates S$90-120k total (Skillup, 2026, aggregator); Hong Kong: no entry-level data found (Road to Offer gives MBA-level base HKD 1.2-1.8m); Tokyo: a Japanese career site says McKinsey Japan new graduates start at roughly ¥5-7m (unverified, third-party).

~5 years (consultant to engagement manager/project leader):
- *US:* total roughly $250-400k for years 2-4 and $350-550k for the manager level (4-6 years) at MBB; Tier 2 about $200-350k and $280-450k (Road to Offer, 2026, a US aggregator; wide ranges).
- *UK:* experienced consultant £65-100k and senior consultant/manager £92-125k across firms (PrepLounge UK, 2026, not firm-specific); MBA/PhD hires at MBB £100-110k base, up to £117-125k total.
- *Italy:* no reliable data found.

Senior (partner): MBB partners are widely said to earn well over $1 million a year (US coaching sources cite $1-5m+); PrepLounge UK gives £200k to £1m+ across all UK firms. Partner pay depends on firm profit; firms do not publish it, so treat as unverified.

path.label: Career path
path.md: Entry titles differ: McKinsey Business Analyst, BCG Associate, Bain Associate Consultant; then Associate/Consultant (often after an MBA or 2-3 years) → Engagement Manager/Project Leader/Case Team Leader (4-7 years) → Associate Partner/Principal → Partner/Director. Expect roughly 2 years per step at the junior levels; promotion is competitive at every step. "Up or out" means people not promoted are typically asked to leave within 1-3 years of the expected promotion date. Most undergraduates do not stay to partner (a small minority, often well under 10%, is a common practitioner estimate; no reliable data found). Many firms sponsor an MBA: you leave for 2 years paid in part and return as a post-MBA Associate/Consultant, usually with an obligation to return; McKinsey Germany has historically offered paid leave for the MBA (e-fellows.net, undated, older). Some firms run a "pre-MBA" analyst programme that ends with the MBA.

exits.label: Exit opportunities
exits.md:
- *After 2-3 years:* MBA (top-10 schools; often sponsored), corporate strategy and business-development roles, private equity associate roles (especially after tier-2 PE-diligence work), tech product/strategy and operations, startups and venture-backed scale-ups.
- *After 7-10 years:* corporate strategy director/VP or business-unit general manager, chief of staff/CSO/COO roles, private-equity operating partner, start-up COO/CEO, founder roles. A coaching site estimates 15-20% of MBB consultants take corporate strategy jobs between years 3 and 8, and calls PE the largest exit by volume (StrategyCase, May 2026; single coach source, unsourced).

tiers.label: Tier list of employers
tiers.md:
*Tier groupings reflect industry consensus and practitioner perception, not objective fact.*
- **Tier 1 (MBB):** McKinsey, BCG, Bain. Highest selectivity, highest pay at entry, broadest alumni network.
- **Tier 1.5/elite specialists:** Oliver Wyman (financial services), Roland Berger (Europe/DACH), Kearney (operations), L.E.K. and OC&C (healthcare/consumer, PE diligence), Simon-Kucher (pricing). Sometimes described as "MBB-adjacent"; pay near MBB in some countries.
- **Tier 2:** Strategy&, EY-Parthenon, Monitor Deloitte, Arthur D. Little, Alvarez & Marsal, AlixPartners, Altman Solon, Capgemini Invent, Accenture Strategy; Big 4 strategy arms sell on the parent's relationships and are heavily used by PE.
- **Tier 3:** Smaller regional strategy boutiques and corporate-strategy arms of IT firms.
- **Differences:** rank follows client prestige, selectivity, alumni destinations and pay, not size.

enter.label: How to enter
enter.md:
- *Degrees/backgrounds:* business, economics, STEM, law, humanities; MBB say they hire from many fields. Strongest evidence is academic distinction plus leadership and quantitative aptitude. In Germany/Austria, McKinsey says fluent German is mandatory (e-fellows.net interview with McKinsey recruiter, 1 Aug 2025), and BCG's round 2 includes a case in German (BCG Germany/Austria, 2026). Roland Berger asks for the local language in every office.
- *Internships/programmes:* summer/spring internships are the main funnel at MBB. BCG's Visiting Associate (8-12 weeks) leads to a binding "FAST FORWARD" offer without further interviews (BCG Germany/Austria careers page, 2026). McKinsey Germany's Fellow Intern is 8-12 weeks (e-fellows.net, 2026). Bain London has no internship programme (Road to Offer UK guide, 2026).
- *Recruiting calendar (2026 cycle; verify on firm sites):*
  - **US:** McKinsey Business Analyst internship deadline 29 March 2026, full-time (undergrad/master's) 11 August 2026; Bain internship 29 March (spring) and 31 August (fall), full-time Associate Consultant 19 July 2026; BCG full-time around 7-14 July 2026 and internships June-September (sources disagree; Tufts/Management Consulted/Road to Offer 2026). Over 60% of interview slots reportedly fill in the first application wave (one analysis; unverified).
  - **UK:** McKinsey portal opened 1 Jan 2026 with a first-round deadline of 29 March, expected to reopen autumn 2026; Bain London reopens in September with first-round cases mid-November (Road to Offer UK, 2026). Rolling review: apply in the first weeks.
  - **DACH:** BCG wants applications at least six months before the start date; McKinsey reviews Fellow Intern applications on a rolling basis (e-fellows.net / BCG, 2026).
  - **Italy:** I could not verify a published calendar for MBB Milan or Rome; check each firm's Italian careers page and university career services.
  - **Gulf/Asia:** campus calendars vary; Singapore and Hong Kong recruit mostly from local and global target universities; no reliable calendar found.
- *Interview formats:* a 20-30 minute online assessment first (McKinsey Solve, BCG's online case/"Casey", Bain's online test), then two or three rounds of case interviews plus a "fit" interview. McKinsey's Solve is a game-style assessment; in 2026 candidate reports describe Redrock Study plus Sea Wolf (about 65 minutes) as the common version, with a longer variant (Management Consulted, Road to Offer and Leland, 2026; third-party descriptions, check your invitation). McKinsey interviews combine a case with a Personal Experience Interview (PEI: a deep behavioural question on leadership, connection, growth and drive; renamed dimensions, summer 2025, third-party). BCG's global process is application → skills (behavioural) interview → case interview → team interview (BCG careers, 2026). Bain describes a recruiter call and several case-interview rounds with objective scoring (Bain, 2026). McKinsey has piloted AI-assisted case interviews (CFO.com citing the FT, Jan 2026).
- *Certifications:* none matter at strategy firms. Language certificates matter in DACH and sometimes Italy.
- *Skills to build:* structured problem-solving (case practice, 30-50 cases is a common recommendation; coaching-industry advice), mental maths, clear writing, Excel; the ability to use AI tools and sanity-check what they say.
- *Common mistakes:* memorising frameworks instead of reasoning; no concrete leadership examples; applying late; underestimating the German requirement; treating internships as optional in DACH.
- *Alternative routes:* non-target schools should use referrals and alumni networking and a master's at a target school; a non-target brand mostly hurts at CV screening, less after that (coaching sources, unverified). Big 4 strategy arms (Monitor Deloitte, Strategy&, EY-Parthenon) are the most common lateral feeders: one coaching firm found over 39% of MBB experienced hires came from other consulting firms (unverified; coaching firm). PhD and "advanced degree" hiring is a separate channel: PhDs typically enter at post-MBA level, up to two years after graduating (coaching sources; check firms). MBA (full-time at a top school) remains the largest route into MBB's higher entry level.
- **Entry difficulty: 5/5**

downsides.label: Honest downsides and who it is NOT a good fit for
downsides.md:
- Long hours and travel in the first years; limited control over staffing; constant evaluation; a pyramid that is no longer growing. Graduate pay has been flat three years running and, per a UK trade piece, real Big 4 pay for new hires has fallen 5-13% depending on the firm (eFinancialCareers via Road to Offer, 2026).
- Much of the junior work is slide-building and data prep; the "strategy" part comes later. AI is shrinking the routine tasks, which can speed up responsibility (good) or reduce hiring (bad).
- Not a fit if you need predictable evenings, dislike constant travel, hate working with ambiguity, or want deep technical craft (engineering, research). Also poor fit if you are in it only for the brand with no interest in business problems; the work is client-facing and political.
- In Italy, local MBB offices are small and pay is unverified; choose carefully if you need Italian-market earning.

roles.title: Management / operations / transformation consultant at Big 4, Accenture and similar

what.label: What you actually do
what.md: You help a client change how it operates and make the change stick. Typical projects: design a new finance operating model for a bank, run a PMO (project management office) for a government digital programme, map and redesign a purchase-to-pay process, lead change management for a new HR system, assess a regulatory-risk framework, or support a cost-reduction programme. Day-to-day: process mapping in Visio/Miro, workshops with client staff, Excel and Power BI analysis, status reports and project plans, and deliverables such as a target operating model, a business case or an implementation roadmap. Compared to strategy, there is more stakeholder management, more documentation and longer project timelines.

day.label: A typical day and week
day.md: Morning: team stand-up, then a workshop with client process owners; midday: update the issue log and timeline; afternoon: client meeting with the programme director; evening: finalise the weekly status deck and next-week plan. Travel to the client site 3-4 days a week is common in the UK, Germany and the US; Italy and Gulf projects are often local or regional. Utilisation targets are tracked (hours billed to clients); weeks between projects ("on the bench") are used for training and internal work.

hours.label: Hours, stress and lifestyle
hours.md:
- *Hours:* typical 45-60 per week; peak 60-70 at go-lives and bid deadlines (StrategyCase, July 2026 suggests Big 4 advisory/strategy 50-65; PrepLounge coach answers; no firm data). The Italian Big 4 are often quoted at long hours for juniors (consumer sites; unverified).
- *Stress:* **3/5.** Steady deadline pressure, occasional high-stakes go-lives and bid work.
- *Lifestyle/flexibility:* more predictable than MBB, with formal flexible-working policies. Staffing can still be demanding, and utilisation targets create pressure to stay on projects.
- *Travel:* moderate to high depending on client location.
- *Remote/hybrid:* hybrid is common; some delivery work is remote or offshore.

profile.label: Human vs. quantitative profile
profile.md: People/communication: 4/5. Quantitative/technical: 3/5. You spend a lot of time persuading client staff to change how they work. Spreadsheet and process analysis skills are needed, but you do not usually need advanced maths.

pay.label: Compensation (approximate)
pay.md:
Entry:
- *US:* Big 4 consulting analyst base: Deloitte $90-100k, KPMG $93-112k, PwC $80-90k, EY $78-91k (Road to Offer, 2026); Accenture Strategy about $105k base (PrepLounge USA, Jan 2026, via earlier research). City premium of $10-20k for New York.
- *UK:* base: Deloitte £37k, PwC £34k, EY £32k, KPMG £32k, Accenture £33.5k; Capgemini Invent £51k (PrepLounge UK, 2026). Other guides give £30-40k for Big 4 in London (LearnSignal and Grant Thornton commentary, 2026). Grant Thornton said Big 4 graduate pay "barely moved in three years" and set its own London pay at £40k from September 2027 (secondary report, 2026).
- *Italy:* no firm-level data found. Indeed shows about €26.6k average for Deloitte Italia "Analyst" and about €28k for Accenture Italia data analyst; a Milan graduate consulting vacancy at Michael Page lists up to €26k; Indeed gives Milan "Consulente" average about €34k across seniority (Indeed Italy, 2026; self-reported, mixed levels). So roughly €26-30k gross entry is the best reading, flagged as indicative.
- *Germany (comparison):* Deloitte about €55k, other Big 4 €50-55k, Accenture about €58k (PrepLounge DACH, Dec 2025).
- *Middle East/Asia:* Dubai Big 4 said to be about 40% below MBB (forum, anecdotal); Singapore Big 4 consulting S$55-70k (Skillup, 2026); Hong Kong Big 4 analyst HKD 500-700k (Road to Offer, 2026).

~5 years (senior consultant/manager): US Big 4 manager base $105-150k (Road to Offer, 2026) and total $200-350k at manager to senior manager level; UK senior consultant/manager £92-125k (all firms, PrepLounge, 2026). Italy: no reliable data found.

Senior (partner/managing director): UK partner pay across firms £200k to £1m+ (PrepLounge UK, 2026); partner equity pay at Big 4 is not published; no reliable data on Italy.

path.label: Career path
path.md: Typical Big 4 ladder: Analyst/Consultant → Senior Consultant → Manager → Senior Manager → Director → Partner. Accenture uses Analyst → Consultant → Manager → Senior Manager → Managing Director. Time per step is about 2 years at the lower levels, 3-4 at manager and above. There is a formal "up or out" at some levels but it is softer than at MBB, with more lateral moves. MBA sponsorship exists but is less common and less generous than at MBB.

exits.label: Exit opportunities
exits.md:
- *After 2-3 years:* move to corporate roles (finance transformation, operations, programme management), switch to another Big 4 line, join a tier-2 strategy firm, start an MBA, or join a vendor/software company.
- *After 7-10 years:* senior manager/director roles in corporates, transformation director or COO in a mid-sized company, partner (rare), or independent consulting/freelance. Lateral hires from Big 4 strategy practices into MBB occur but the route is narrow and mostly from the strategy arms.

tiers.label: Tier list of employers
tiers.md:
*Tier groupings reflect industry consensus and practitioner perception, not objective fact.*
- **Big 4 strategy arms (closest to tier 2):** Strategy& (PwC), EY-Parthenon, Monitor Deloitte, KPMG strategy group: stronger selectivity and higher pay.
- **Big 4 management/operations/risk practices:** Deloitte Consulting (largest advisory business), PwC Advisory, EY Consulting, KPMG Advisory.
- **Accenture:** the largest pure consulting-and-technology firm (FY2026 revenue $74.2bn; about 779,000 staff at last confirmed count after 2025 cuts).
- **Other large consultancies:** Capgemini, Cognizant, IBM Consulting, Infosys Consulting, Sopra Steria, plus regional firms such as BIP and Reply in Italy.
- **Differences:** these firms recruit more widely (many universities, more roles per year), pay less at entry than strategy firms, and offer broader exposure and longer implementation work.

enter.label: How to enter
enter.md:
- *Degrees/backgrounds:* business, economics, engineering, IT, supply chain, social sciences. Most graduate programmes are open to all disciplines.
- *Programmes:* spring weeks/insight programmes (UK), summer internships, graduate schemes. UK Big 4 recruitment is rolling and opens in September (Deloitte deadline 1 May 2026, PwC 1 June 2026, EY and KPMG 24 April 2026, but seats close early; Road to Offer UK, 2026). Accenture opens its graduate programmes in August-September (Road to Offer / aggregators).
- *Interview formats:* online application, situational judgement test, numerical/verbal reasoning (SHL-type), video interview, assessment centre with case study, group exercise and interview; Deloitte immersive assessment (about 40 SJT-style questions) (Road to Offer UK, 2026). Case interviews are lighter than at MBB.
- *Certifications:* PMP, Prince2, Lean Six Sigma, Agile (Scrum) and vendor certifications (SAP, Salesforce, ServiceNow) can help at the margin for operations and implementation roles but are rarely required at graduate entry; employers often pay for them later.
- *Skills to build:* Excel/Power BI, process mapping, project management basics, clear business writing, stakeholder skills.
- *Common mistakes:* assuming it is easy (acceptance rates are lower than the number of openings suggests; no reliable published figures); not tailoring to the service line; ignoring intake cuts and expecting a safe fallback.
- *Alternative routes:* internal transfers from audit or tax; apprenticeships in the UK; experienced hires from industry; Big 4 to MBB lateral for strategy-arm people.
- **Entry difficulty: 3/5**

downsides.label: Honest downsides and who it is NOT a good fit for
downsides.md:
- Lower entry pay than strategy; intake cuts and AI pressure mean this is no longer a guaranteed safety net (PwC US plan, PwC UK, Accenture cuts above). Work can be repetitive (documentation, PMO reporting), and utilisation targets can feel like a timesheet culture.
- Not a fit if you want to do original strategic analysis from day one, if you dislike process and change-management work, or if you struggle with bureaucracy.
- In Italy entry pay is low relative to cost of living in Milan (indicative €26-30k gross), though this is typical of the Italian graduate market (Mercer puts Italian first-job pay at about €30.5k for 2024, as cited by Sky TG24, 2025).

compare.name: Management/operations/transformation at Big 4, Accenture
compare.pay: US: $78-112k base (Big 4 analyst; Accenture Strategy ~$105k); UK: £32-37k base (2026); Italy: ~€26-30k gross (indicative, Indeed/Michael Page 2026)

summary: US: $78-112k base (Big 4 analyst; Accenture Strategy ~$105k); UK: £32-37k base (2026); Italy: ~€26-30k gross (indicative, Indeed/Michael Page 2026)

roles.title: Specialist / boutique consultant (sector or function specialists)

what.label: What you actually do
what.md: You advise on one sector or function, using deep content. At a healthcare and life-sciences boutique (for example L.E.K., ZS, ClearView) you might size a drug's market, build a revenue forecast, interview doctors and payers, and write a launch strategy; at a pricing specialist (Simon-Kucher) you design a price architecture and test willingness to pay with customer surveys; at a sustainability or energy boutique you model decarbonisation pathways and help with disclosure; at a restructuring/performance-improvement firm (A&M, AlixPartners) you may build a 13-week cash-flow forecast for a distressed company and help run the turnaround. Tools: Excel and PowerPoint, specialist databases, survey tools, sometimes SQL or Python. Deliverables: models, market reports, due-diligence memos and implementation plans.

day.label: A typical day and week
day.md: Similar to strategy but more content-driven: morning on data and calls with sector experts; afternoon building a model; evening on a deck for the partner. Due-diligence projects (PE-sponsored commercial diligence) run 3-6 weeks with heavy hours; longer retainer projects are steadier. Many boutiques have a smaller team (3-5) and more direct partner contact, so juniors take on client exposure earlier.

hours.label: Hours, stress and lifestyle
hours.md:
- *Hours:* typical 50-65 per week; peaks 70-80 on PE due diligence or restructuring (StrategyCase, July 2026: boutiques 45-70; wide variation by firm and practice).
- *Stress:* **4/5** in due-diligence and restructuring boutiques; **3/5** in many sector and pricing practices.
- *Lifestyle/flexibility:* depends heavily on the firm; some boutiques offer better balance than MBB, others work PE timelines.
- *Travel:* usually lower than MBB in Europe; high in US consulting boutiques.
- *Remote/hybrid:* hybrid common.

profile.label: Human vs. quantitative profile
profile.md: People/communication: 3/5. Quantitative/technical: 4/5. Specialist work is usually more modelling- and data-heavy (healthcare forecasting, pricing analytics), and clients value your content knowledge more than your presentation polish.

pay.label: Compensation (approximate)
pay.md:
Entry:
- *UK:* L.E.K. £50,000 base (up to ~£54k total), OC&C £51,000 (up to £58k), Simon-Kucher £52,000 (up to £55k), Altman Solon £50,000 (up to £56k), ClearView £50,000 (up to £54k), ZS £47,000 (up to £51.5k), Arthur D. Little £40,000, Alvarez & Marsal £35,000 (up to £41k), FTI £40,000, Kearney £41,000, Oliver Wyman £34,000 (PrepLounge UK, 2026; these figures conflict with other sources, which place Oliver Wyman and Kearney closer to MBB, so treat London tier-2 numbers as a range and check the offer).
- *US:* Oliver Wyman undergraduate analysts $95-132k; L.E.K. MBA base $110-180k (Road to Offer, 2026; US bonus 20-30% at L.E.K.).
- *Germany:* Kearney about €80k base, Simon-Kucher €68k, Roland Berger €72k, Oliver Wyman about €60.5k (PrepLounge DACH, Dec 2025, single source).
- *Italy:* no reliable data found for sector boutiques. Indirect: Oliver Wyman Italy about €43k base (Management Consulted 2026, single source, via earlier research); Alvarez & Marsal Spain €50k base (same). Treat Italian boutique pay as likely above Big 4 entry level but unverified.
- *Gulf/Asia:* Dubai tier-2 and boutique packages are reported around AED 22-25k per month for strategy houses (forum, unverified); Singapore: PrepLounge says non-MBB strategy firms offer analyst packages in a similar range to MBB, with the gap opening later (summarised from PrepLounge Singapore, 2026).

~5 years: approximately US $200-350k total at the 2-4 year consultant level and $280-450k at manager for tier-2 firms (Road to Offer, 2026); UK experienced consultant £65-100k; Italy no reliable data.

Senior: specialist practice leaders and partners can earn as much as strategy partners at top boutiques; no reliable published data.

path.label: Career path
path.md: Analyst/Associate → Consultant → Senior Consultant/Engagement Manager → Principal/Director → Partner. Boutiques often promote faster and give earlier responsibility, but promotion pools are smaller and the firm may be sold or restructured (many boutiques have been acquired by larger groups). MBA sponsorship exists at some, less systematically than at MBB.

exits.label: Exit opportunities
exits.md:
- *After 2-3 years:* move into the industry you advised (pharma strategy, retail pricing, energy), private equity or venture (especially from PE-diligence boutiques), larger strategy firms or a business school.
- *After 7-10 years:* director or VP roles in the sector, partner at the boutique, or an operating role in a PE-owned company. Specialist knowledge makes you hireable but can limit the breadth of moves compared with MBB generalists.

tiers.label: Tier list of employers
tiers.md:
*Tier groupings reflect industry consensus and practitioner perception, not objective fact.*
- **Top specialists (near tier-2 prestige):** L.E.K. (healthcare, PE diligence), OC&C (consumer), Simon-Kucher (pricing), Oliver Wyman (financial services), Kearney (operations), Altman Solon (telecom, media, tech), Roland Berger.
- **Strong functional specialists:** Alvarez & Marsal, AlixPartners, FTI Consulting (restructuring and performance improvement), ZS and other pharma-commercial consultancies.
- **Smaller regional and national boutiques:** in Italy, BIP, Value Partners and The European House - Ambrosetti are examples; their size and prestige vary and were not verified beyond headcounts quoted above.
- **Differences:** sector depth, case-led interviews, and clientele (PE and corporates).

enter.label: How to enter
enter.md:
- *Degrees/backgrounds:* the sector helps: life sciences or medicine for healthcare consulting, engineering or economics for energy and operations, finance or economics for restructuring. Many boutiques hire generalists and train them.
- *Programmes:* graduate and analyst programmes, internships; many boutiques recruit year-round, with timing mirroring PE cycles. Applications are often direct and less formal than MBB.
- *Interview formats:* case interviews (often more data/modelling heavy and sector-specific), fit interviews; some firms add Excel tests and written exercises.
- *Certifications:* mostly not required; CFA is rarely needed outside restructuring and finance-heavy boutiques; project management certifications are marginal.
- *Skills to build:* modelling, sector knowledge, written communication.
- *Common mistakes:* applying with no evidence of interest in the sector; assuming boutiques are easier (healthcare and PE boutiques are very selective).
- *Alternative routes:* PhD/MD/PharmD hires for life-sciences consulting; lateral moves from industry; Big 4 or internal teams into specialist practices.
- **Entry difficulty: 4/5** for the top specialists (L.E.K., OC&C, Simon-Kucher, Oliver Wyman); 3/5 for smaller national boutiques.

downsides.label: Honest downsides and who it is NOT a good fit for
downsides.md:
- Smaller firms have thinner training and brand; pay is less transparent and varies more; exits can be tied to the sector. Smaller bench means you can be staffed on the wrong sector for years.
- PE-driven work can be as intense as MBB, with weekend crunches.
- Not a fit if you want a broad generalist's CV and flexibility in what you do next, or if you dislike committing to a sector early.
